content: # Thinking with Models: companion app # One inquiry in six steps. The reader finds where two explanations of blocking # disagree, examines what the disagreement depends on, designs and runs a # simulated experiment, decides what its records support, and meets the same # question in a different model. Explore lets the reader change the settings # freely. # # Files in R/ are loaded by Shiny before this one: # models.R the learning models (a copy of R/models.R; the tests require # the two to be identical) # engine.R the model calculations, except the experiments of Step 5; # checked by tests/verify_app.R # formulas.R displayed model equations and symbol definitions # helpers.R shared text, number formats and small building blocks # ask.R questions, locked answers, and notes # plots.R figures # opening.R the opening and the step buttons # training.R Step 1 # comparison.R Step 2 # assumptions.R Step 3 # responses.R Step 4 # experiment.R Step 5 (records from data/inference_cases.rds, # written by shiny_app/make_inference_cases.R) # decision.R Step 6 # explore.R the Explore tab # values.R the model results the page shows, computed once at startup # tests/verify_app_flow.R walks through the six steps of the inquiry. # # Requirements: shiny, bslib, ggplot2 # Launch from the repository root: shiny::runApp("shiny_app") library(shiny) library(bslib) library(ggplot2) # UI # The steps with the notes beside them. On narrow screens the notes come after # the steps, and a small fixed link jumps there. with_notes <- function(content) div(class = "layout", div(class = "main part", content), div(class = "notes", id = "notes_box", tags$details(id = "notes_details", open = NA, tags$summary(h2("Your notes")), downloadLink("notes_download", "Download notes (.txt)"), uiOutput("notes"))), tags$a(class = "notes-jump", href = "#notes_box", "Notes")) about <- div(class = "part", h2(class = "about", "About this page"), p(HTML("You can work through this page without reading the accompanying tutorial, Thinking with Models through Simulation to Guide Scientific Inquiry by Kenny Yu (KU Leuven). Both use the same blocking example to compare the Rescorla–Wagner and adaptive-associability models.")), p("For the derivations, code checks and full simulation study, follow the references marked “In the tutorial” or inspect the R scripts in the repository linked below."), h3("Where the numbers come from"), p("Steps 1 to 4 and Explore calculate the model predictions as you use the page. Step 6 calculates accuracy and decision times from the diffusion model. The numerical checks compare these results with the tutorial."), p("Step 5 uses saved simulated experiments from the tutorial's study. Changing the sample size or the recorded presentations selects the corresponding data and analysis; no models are fitted while you use the page."), p("The individual cases use one generating parameter set. The percentages shown at the end summarize 400 experiments per design: 100 under each of four parameter sets."), tags$details(class = "formula-details", tags$summary("Code and numerical checks"), P("The learning calculations use shiny_app/R/models.R, an identical copy of R/models.R used in the tutorial. Step 6 uses shiny_app/R/engine.R. tests/verify_app.R checks both against the reported values, including B's learned value of ", num(trained$rw$V_B, 4), " under ", RW, " after compound training, and the adaptive model's B–D gap of ", num(at(base$adaptive$gap, 8)), " after eight updates."), P("For Step 5, shiny_app/make_inference_cases.R regenerates one experiment of each size per generating process from saved random seeds. It analyzes every design with the study's code and stops if a result disagrees with the corresponding saved study analysis. These cases use the first parameter set.")), p(HTML(paste0("Code and materials: ", "github.com/kennychechuanyu/thinking_with_simulations."))) ) ui <- page_fixed( theme = bs_theme(version = 5, bg = "#FFFFFF", fg = "#252525", primary = "#252525", base_font = font_collection("Charter", "Georgia", "Cambria", "serif"), heading_font = font_collection("Charter", "Georgia", "serif")), title = "Thinking with Models", tags$head(tags$link(rel = "stylesheet", href = "style.css"), tags$script(src = "scenes.js"), # The link in Step 3's matched-control question opens Explore at its results. # It waits until the tab is shown and the starting states have been drawn. tags$script(HTML(" document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler('show_explore', function (m) { document.getElementById('control-e').open = true; var tries = 0; (function scrollWhenDrawn() { var results = document.querySelector('.explore-output'); var states = document.getElementById('x_summary'); if (results && results.offsetParent !== null && states && states.textContent.trim()) results.scrollIntoView(); else if (++tries < 100) setTimeout(scrollWhenDrawn, 50); })(); }); Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler('scroll_top', function (m) { var heading = document.querySelector('.opening'); if (heading) { heading.setAttribute('tabindex', '-1'); heading.focus({ preventScroll: true }); } window.scrollTo(0, 0); }); });"))), div(class = "masthead", h1("Thinking with Models"), p("Two learning models explain blocking. What would you try next?")), navset_underline(id = "tabs", nav_panel("The inquiry", with_notes(tagList(opening_ui(), training_ui(), comparison_ui(), assumptions_ui(), responses_ui(), experiment_ui(), decision_ui()))), nav_panel("Explore", explore_ui()), nav_panel("About", about)) ) # Server server <- function(input, output, session) { # The saved answer to each question, and the entries of the notes. answers <- reactiveValues() entries <- reactiveVal(list()) add_note <- function(...) entries(c(entries(), list(note(...)))) # A logical output read by conditionalPanel. The "..." lets both Shiny and # shiny::testServer call it. The flags that complete Steps 1 to 5 also go # to scenes.js, which marks the step complete. flag <- function(name, condition) { output[[name]] <- function(...) condition() outputOptions(output, name, suspendWhenHidden = FALSE) if (name %in% c("done_q1", "done_q2", "done_q3c", "done_q4b", "done_e6")) observe(session$sendCustomMessage("scene_done", list(name = name, done = isTRUE(condition())))) } # One flag per question, done_q1 and so on: TRUE once it has been answered. for (id in c("q1", "q2", "q2b", "q3a", "q3b", "q3c", "q3d", "q6", "q4a", "q4b", "e_design", "e1", "e2", "e3", "e4", "e5", "e6", "x1", "x2", "x3")) local({ i <- id; flag(paste0("done_", i), function() !is.null(answers[[i]])) }) output$notes <- renderUI(notes_ui(entries())) output$notes_download <- downloadHandler( filename = function() paste0("thinking-with-models-notes-", Sys.Date(), ".txt"), content = function(file) writeLines(notes_text(entries()), file)) training <- training_server(input, output, answers, add_note) comparison <- comparison_server(input, output, answers, add_note) assumptions <- assumptions_server(input, output, answers, add_note) responses <- responses_server(input, output, answers, add_note) experiment <- experiment_server(input, output, answers, add_note, flag) decision <- decision_server(input, output, answers, add_note) explore <- explore_server(input, output, session) # The link in Step 3's matched-control question opens Explore at the default # settings, with E one part in a million more salient than D. observeEvent(input$q6_explore, { explore$defaults() updateRadioButtons(session, "x_e", selected = "1e-6") nav_select("tabs", "Explore", session = session) session$sendCustomMessage("show_explore", TRUE) }) # Trying another design or case clears the answers of Steps 5 and 6, since # Step 6 opens only after Step 5. The notes are kept. observeEvent(input$e_again, { experiment$reset(); decision$reset() }) # Starting again clears the answers of every step and keeps the notes. observeEvent(input$restart, { training$reset(); comparison$reset(); assumptions$reset(); responses$reset() experiment$reset(); decision$reset() session$sendCustomMessage("scroll_top", TRUE) }) } shinyApp(ui, server)

content: # Step 3: what the prediction depends on (Sections 4.3 and 4.5) # The reader's conclusion so far, then the three assumptions behind the curves # of Step 2. Old-value carryover comes first, after which the reader may change # the conclusion; associability carryover and the exactly matched control are # further explorations. assumptions_ui <- function() { scene("scene-3", "3", "What does the prediction depend on?", "output.done_q2", "done_q3c", "Old-value carryover gives Rescorla–Wagner a B–D gap too. When the gap appears may help distinguish the explanations.", P("The two models gave different learning curves for O2. Those curves used three starting assumptions:"), tags$ul( tags$li(HTML(paste0("Both cues start with no learned value for O2 (no old-value carryover, ", gV, " = 0). Their values for O1 do not set their starting values for O2."))), tags$li(HTML(paste0("In the adaptive model, each cue keeps the associability it reached during O1 training (full associability carryover, ", gA, " = 1)."))), tags$li(HTML(paste0("The control cues D and E are exactly equally salient, so that D's associability stays at ", num(trained$adaptive$alpha_D), ".")))), p("The adaptive prediction also depends on this model's particular rule for updating associability. After revising your conclusion, you can test a slight mismatch between D and E in “Explore further: control-cue salience” below."), carryover_formulas_ui(), p("If D learned more than B about O2, what would you conclude? Save your answer, then try allowing some old value to carry over. These settings show what follows from an assumption; data would still be needed to judge what real learners carry over."), div(class = "question", uiOutput("q3a")), conditionalPanel("output.done_q3a", # Old-value carryover tagList( h3("Allow some old value to carry over"), P("Suppose part of what the learner expects from O1 also affects its expectation of O2. Set each cue's O2 starting value to a fraction ", gV, " of its final O1 value: .5 keeps half, and 1 keeps all. At the end of compound training, ", RW, " left B at ", num(trained$rw$V_B), " and D at ", num(trained$rw$V_D), "."), div(class = "question", uiOutput("q3b")), conditionalPanel("output.done_q3b", P("Try a few values of ", gV, ". This changes the starting values in both models; associability still carries over in full. Look at the gap before any O2 feedback, as well as the gap during learning."), sliderInput("gv", HTML(paste0("Old-value carryover, ", gV)), min = 0, max = 1, value = .5, step = .05, ticks = FALSE, width = "320px"), uiOutput("gv_text"), fig("p3_gap", "280px"), fig("p3_grid", "280px"), p(class = "muted", "The open circle is the adaptive model at the Step 2 setting, with no old-value carryover. As more old value carries over, the adaptive model's gap after eight updates becomes smaller, because both cues begin with higher predictions about O2 and leave less error for their different associabilities to act on."), aside("Section 4.3."), div(class = "question", uiOutput("q3c_claim"), uiOutput("q3c")))), # Associability carryover conditionalPanel("output.done_q3c", tags$details(class = "further", tags$summary("Explore further: associability carryover"), h3("Only part of the associability change carries over"), P("Now vary how much of the associability change carries over. With ", gA, " = 1, B enters O2 at ", num(trained$adaptive$alpha_B), " and D at ", num(trained$adaptive$alpha_D), ". With ", gA, " = 0, both return to the original baseline of .5. A setting of .5 keeps half of the change from baseline, rather than half of the associability itself. Here, old-value carryover is 0, so both cues start O2 at value 0."), div(class = "question", uiOutput("q3d")), conditionalPanel("output.done_q3d", sliderInput("ga", HTML(paste0("Associability carryover, ", gA)), min = 0, max = 1, value = .5, step = .05, ticks = FALSE, width = "320px"), uiOutput("ga_text"), fig("p3_ga", "280px"), aside("Section 4.3."))), # The exactly matched control tags$details(id = "control-cue-salience", class = "further", tags$summary("Explore further: control-cue salience"), h3("How closely must the control cues match?"), P("D's associability stayed at ", num(trained$adaptive$alpha_D), " because D and E made exactly the same error on every compound trial."), div(class = "question", uiOutput("q6")))))) } assumptions_server <- function(input, output, answers, add_note) { # The conclusion so far claim_choices <- c( support = "If an experiment finds D ahead of B on the new outcome, that supports the adaptive model over Rescorla–Wagner.", depends = "The models disagree under these assumptions. Whether a B–D difference supports the adaptive model depends on what carries over to the new task.", none = "The two explanations cannot be told apart.") q3a_items <- list(item("claim", "What would you conclude so far?", claim_choices)) ask_server("q3a", input, output, answers, q3a_items, button = "Save my conclusion", feedback = function(a) p("Your notes now keep this conclusion. See whether you would keep it after allowing some old value to carry over."), on_submit = function(a) add_note("Step 3", "Initial conclusion", "Which conclusion would you draw after Step 2?", claim_choices[[a$claim]], settings = first_set())) # Old-value carryover when_choices <- c(before = "Already before the first O2 trial.", after = "Only after some O2 trials.", none = "There is no gap.") q3b_items <- list( item("dir", paste0("If some old value carries over, what will ", RW, " predict for the B–D gap?"), gap_choices), item("when", "If there is a gap, when does it first appear?", when_choices)) ask_server("q3b", input, output, answers, q3b_items, reason = "What makes you think so? (optional)", button = "See what changes", feedback = function(a) tagList( if (a$dir == "zero") p("Equal starting values gave no gap in Step 2. Here, the same positive fraction of two unequal O1 values is carried over, so their O2 starting values are unequal too.") else if (a$dir == "neg") p("B finished O1 training below D. Keeping the same fraction of each old value preserves that order, so it cannot put B ahead at the start of O2."), P(RW, " now puts D ahead of B. B ended compound training at ", num(trained$rw$V_B), " and D at ", num(trained$rw$V_D), ", so with any carryover D starts the new task higher."), if (a$when != "before") p("Carryover sets the values before learning the new outcome. The first response can therefore show a gap before any O2 feedback has occurred."), P("The gap is there before any O2 feedback. After that it shrinks: both cues use the same multiplier, and B, which is farther from 1, gains more on each trial.")), on_submit = function(a) add_note("Step 3", "Old-value carryover", paste0("With old-value carryover, what does ", RW, " predict?"), paste0(gap_choices[[a$dir]], " ", when_choices[[a$when]], if (nzchar(a$reason)) paste0(" Reason: ", a$reason)), result = paste0("D ahead from the start. At ", gV, " = 1 the gap after eight updates is ", num(at(gv1$rw$gap, 8)), " (", RW, ") and ", num(at(gv1$adaptive$gap, 8)), " (adaptive model). The two are equal near ", gV, " = ", num(gv_cross), "."), settings = paste0(first_set(), "; vary g_V from 0 to 1"))) gv_run <- reactive(run_inquiry(settings_with(g_V = input$gv))) output$gv_text <- renderUI({ req(answers$q3b) r <- gv_run(); g <- input$gv P("With ", gV, " = ", axis_num(g), ", ", if (g == 0) "B and D both start at 0 for O2, so neither model has a gap before any O2 feedback. " else paste0("the gap before any O2 feedback is already ", num(at(r$rw$gap, 0)), " under ", RW, " (B starts at ", num(at(r$rw$B$V, 0)), ", D at ", num(at(r$rw$D$V, 0)), ") and ", num(at(r$adaptive$gap, 0)), " under the adaptive model. "), "After eight updates the gaps are ", prob(at(r$rw$gap, 8)), " (", RW, ") and ", num(at(r$adaptive$gap, 8)), " (adaptive model). Above about ", gV, " = ", num(gv_cross), ", ", RW, " predicts the larger gap after eight updates.", if (g > 0) " Gaps are calculated from unrounded values.") }) output$p3_gap <- renderPlot({ req(answers$q3b) plot_gap(gv_run(), ylim = c(-.02, .35), title = paste0("The B–D gap with old-value carryover of ", axis_num(input$gv))) }) output$p3_grid <- renderPlot({ req(answers$q3b) plot_gap_by_gV(gv_grid, input$gv, cross = gv_cross) }) output$q3c_claim <- renderUI({ req(answers$q3a) if (!is.null(answers$q3c)) return(NULL) tagList(p(class = "item-label", "Earlier you chose this conclusion:"), tags$blockquote(HTML(claim_choices[[answers$q3a$claim]]))) }) revise_choices <- c( keep = "Keep it as it is.", qualify = "Under the first assumptions the explanations predict different B–D gaps. Once old learned values may carry over, a positive gap alone no longer tells them apart. When the gap first appears may still help.", useless = "The comparison is useless, because both explanations can produce the gap.") q3c_items <- list(item("rev", "Would you keep your earlier conclusion or change it?", revise_choices)) ask_server("q3c", input, output, answers, q3c_items, reason = "You can also put the conclusion in your own words", button = "Save my conclusion", feedback = function(a) { earlier <- answers$q3a$claim tagList( p(class = "answered-label", "Your earlier conclusion"), tags$blockquote(HTML(claim_choices[[earlier]])), P(switch(a$rev, keep = switch(earlier, support = paste0("With old-value carryover, ", RW, " also puts D ahead of B, and above about ", gV, " = ", num(gv_cross), " its gap is the larger one after eight updates. A B–D difference alone no longer favors the adaptive model."), depends = paste0("Your earlier conclusion already allowed for this. The simulation shows one way it matters: old-value carryover gives ", RW, " a gap too."), none = "Under the first assumptions the explanations disagree. With old-value carryover both start with a gap, so the size of a difference alone does not tell them apart. A gap from old values is there before any O2 feedback. A gap from associability, with equal starting values, appears only after O2 feedback. So when the gap first appears may still help."), qualify = "A gap from old values is present before O2 feedback; a gap from associability develops during O2 learning. Recording the first response lets you check for this distinction. Whether the responses show it also depends on how learned values become answers.", useless = paste0("You can still use the timing of the gap. With old-value carryover, ", RW, "'s gap is largest before any O2 feedback and then shrinks. With no old-value carryover, the adaptive model's gap starts at zero and grows over the first updates. To examine that distinction, you need records from the first presentation and a response measure that can express it.")))) }, on_submit = function(a) { g <- input$gv; r <- gv_run() add_note("Step 3", "Revised conclusion", "Would you keep or change your conclusion?", paste0("Before: ", claim_choices[[answers$q3a$claim]], " After: ", revise_choices[[a$rev]], if (nzchar(a$reason)) paste0(" Your own version: ", a$reason)), result = paste0("With ", gV, " = 0: ", RW, " gap ", prob(at(base$rw$gap, 8)), " and adaptive gap ", num(at(base$adaptive$gap, 8)), " after eight updates. With ", gV, " = ", axis_num(g), ", the value you were looking at: ", RW, " gap ", prob(at(r$rw$gap, 0)), " before any O2 feedback and ", prob(at(r$rw$gap, 8)), " after eight updates, adaptive gap ", num(at(r$adaptive$gap, 8)), " after eight updates."), settings = paste0(first_set(settings_with(g_V = g)), "; compared with g_V = 0"), open = "Real learners may carry over old values, associability, both, or neither.") }) # Associability carryover q3d_items <- list(item("h", paste0("If only half of the associability change is kept (", gA, " = .5), what happens to the adaptive model's gap on the first update?"), c( half = "It is half as large.", gone = "It disappears.", same = "It is unchanged."))) ask_server("q3d", input, output, answers, q3d_items, button = "See what changes", feedback = function(a) tagList( if (a$h == "gone") p("Keeping half of the change moves B's associability halfway back to baseline; it does not reset it completely. D is already at baseline, so the two still begin O2 with different associabilities.") else if (a$h == "same") p("The first O2 update uses the associability carried into the task. B now enters the new task at ", num(ga_half$start$alpha_B), " instead of ", num(trained$adaptive$alpha_B), ", and the first gap is the fixed salience, .3, times the difference in associability. With no carryover at all, B and D enter at the same associability and the gap is zero throughout. The learning rule does not determine how much carries over to O2. That fraction has to be specified separately.")), on_submit = function(a) add_note("Step 3", "Associability carryover", q3d_items[[1]]$label, q3d_items[[1]]$choices[[a$h]], result = paste0("First gap ", num(at(base$adaptive$gap, 1)), " with full carryover, ", num(at(ga_half$adaptive$gap, 1)), " with half, 0 with none."), settings = paste0(first_set(), "; compare g_alpha = 1, .5 and 0"))) ga_run <- reactive(run_inquiry(settings_with(g_alpha = input$ga))) output$ga_text <- renderUI({ req(answers$q3d) r <- ga_run(); g <- input$ga P("With ", gA, " = ", axis_num(g), ", B enters the new task at ", num(r$start$alpha_B), " and D at ", num(r$start$alpha_D), ". The gap is ", prob(at(r$adaptive$gap, 1)), " after the first update and ", prob(at(r$adaptive$gap, 8)), " after eight.") }) output$p3_ga <- renderPlot({ req(answers$q3d) plot_gap(ga_run(), ylim = c(-.02, .32), ref = base, ref_label = "Full carryover", title = paste0("B–D gap, associability carryover of ", axis_num(input$ga))) }) # The exactly matched control gap8 <- function(r) at(r$adaptive$gap, 8) # How the gap after eight updates compares with the exactly matched control's: # below half counts as much smaller, above double as much larger. e_change <- function(r) { ratio <- gap8(r) / gap8(base) if (ratio < .5) "smaller" else if (ratio > 2) "larger" else "same" } e_choices <- c(same = "About the same.", smaller = "Much smaller.", larger = "Much larger.") q6_items <- list(item("c", "If E is one part in a million more salient than D, what happens to the B–D gap after eight updates?", e_choices)) e_row <- function(label, r) tags$tr(tags$td(label), tags$td(num(r$trained$adaptive$alpha_D)), tags$td(num(gap8(r)))) ask_server("q6", input, output, answers, q6_items, feedback = function(a) { tagList( if (a$c != e_change(e_up)) p("A tiny salience difference makes D's error differ from E's by a tiny amount. This rule changes associability in proportion to the difference between the errors, so D's associability changes by a similarly tiny amount."), P("The gap stays about the same. With E one part in a million more salient, D's associability after compound training and the gap after eight updates each change by less than one millionth."), p(class = "table-note", "Adaptive model, no old-value carryover"), tags$table(class = "values", tags$thead(tags$tr(tags$th("Salience of E"), tags$th("D's associability"), tags$th("Gap after eight updates"))), tags$tbody(e_row("Same as D", base), e_row("One part in a million higher", e_up), e_row("One part in a million lower", e_down))), p("A rule that uses only which cue predicts better could give a large effect even for a tiny mismatch. Here, the size of the error difference controls the size of the associability change. The matching assumption therefore needs to be read together with the update rule."), p(actionLink("q6_explore", "Open Explore with E one part in a million more salient")), aside("Section 4.5 and Supplement S3.")) }, on_submit = function(a) add_note("Step 3", "The matched control", q6_items[[1]]$label, e_choices[[a$c]], result = paste0("D's associability after compound training ", num(base$trained$adaptive$alpha_D), " with equal salience, ", num(e_up$trained$adaptive$alpha_D), " with E more salient, ", num(e_down$trained$adaptive$alpha_D), " with E less salient. Gap after eight updates ", num(gap8(base)), ", ", num(gap8(e_up)), " and ", num(gap8(e_down)), "."), settings = paste0(first_set(), "; compare E salience offsets +1e-6 and -1e-6"))) # Starting the inquiry again clears the answers but keeps the notes. list(reset = function() clear_answers(answers, c("q3a", "q3b", "q3c", "q3d", "q6"))) }

# Step 2: where the two models would disagree (Sections 3.3 and 3.4)
# The four comparisons the reader can try, one at a time. Training on a new
# outcome, O2, leads to the prediction for O2, its learning curves, one update
# in detail, and why the gap narrows.

comparison_ui <- function() {
  scene("scene-2", "2", "Where would the models disagree?", "output.done_q1", "done_q2",
    "With equal starting values for a new outcome, the adaptive model predicts slower learning for B than for D; Rescorla–Wagner predicts no difference.",
    p("B finishes training with a lower value than D. The adaptive model also gives
       B a lower associability. How could you examine that difference in how readily
       the cues learn? Choose a comparison and say what you hope to learn from it.
       If it does not isolate that difference, you can try another."),
    div(class = "question", uiOutput("cmp"), uiOutput("cmp_msg", role = "status")))
}


comparison_server <- function(input, output, answers, add_note) {

  # The comparisons, tried one at a time. After more training ("more"),
  # continued training with O1 ("cont") or the comparison across models
  # ("across"), the reader says whether it isolates the difference in how readily
  # B and D learn. The new outcome ("new") leads to the prediction for O2, after
  # which no further comparison is offered.
  cmp_label <- "Which comparison would you run?"
  cmp_choices <- c(
    more = "Give more compound training and compare B's and D's final learned values.",
    cont = "Keep training B and D with the same outcome, each alone, and compare their learning.",
    across = "Compare the two models' learned values for B after training.",
    new = "Train B and D on a new outcome, from the same starting value, and compare how quickly each learns.")
  tells_label <- "Does this comparison isolate the difference in how readily B and D learn?"
  tells_choices <- c(yes = "Yes.", no = "No.")

  cmp_result <- list(
    more = tagList(
      p(class = "table-note", "Learned value for O1 at the end of compound training"),
      tags$table(class = "values", cue_head("Compound trials"),
        tags$tbody(
          vrow(RW, n_base, num(trained$rw$V_B), num(trained$rw$V_D)),
          vrow(RW, n_more, num(more$rw$V_B), num(more$rw$V_D)),
          vrow("Adaptive model", n_base, num(trained$adaptive$V_B), num(trained$adaptive$V_D)),
          vrow("Adaptive model", n_more, num(more$adaptive$V_B), num(more$adaptive$V_D))))),
    cont = tagList(
      p(class = "table-note", "Ten more trials with O1, each cue alone, starting from the values
                               that compound training left"),
      fig("p_cont_curves", "300px"),
      fig("p_cont_gap", "260px")),
    across = tagList(
      p(class = "table-note", "B at the end of compound training, and the multiplier on the
                               first compound trial"),
      tags$table(class = "values",
        tags$thead(tags$tr(tags$th("Model"), tags$th("B's learned value"),
                           tags$th("First multiplier"))),
        tags$tbody(
          vrow(RW, num(trained$rw$V_B), num(trained$rw$mult_first)),
          vrow("Adaptive model", num(trained$adaptive$V_B), num(trained$adaptive$mult_first))))),
    new = tagList(
      p("Give B and D ten trials each on their own, now followed by a new outcome,
         O2 (for example, a different kind of food). Start both cues at value 0 for O2.
         In the adaptive model, keep the associabilities left by O1 training."),
      design_table(third = TRUE),
      p("The B–D gap is D's value minus B's.
         A positive gap means D has learned more. What do you expect each model to predict?"),
      div(class = "question inner", uiOutput("q2")),
      conditionalPanel("output.done_q2",
        fig("p2_curves", "300px"),
        fig("p2_gap", "280px"),
        tags$details(
          tags$summary("Look inside one update"),
          p("Choose an update to check the calculation. Multiply the error by the
             multiplier to get the gain, then add it to the value before the update."),
          div(class = "controls-inline",
            radioButtons("t_model", "Model", inline = TRUE,
                         choiceNames = list("Adaptive model", HTML(RW)),
                         choiceValues = c("adaptive", "rw")),
            sliderInput("t_k", "Update number", min = 1, max = 10, value = 1, step = 1,
                        ticks = FALSE, width = "260px")),
          uiOutput("trial_table"),
          uiOutput("trial_note"),
          div(class = "question inner", uiOutput("q2b"))),
        aside("Sections 3.3 and 3.4."))))

  tells_text <- list(
    more = paste0("B remains below D after ", n_more, " compound trials in both models.
      More training has preserved blocking. The numerical predictions differ, but they
      depend on both the error rule and the chosen learning rates. You still cannot
      separate a change in how readily B learns from those other differences."),
    cont = paste0("D stays ahead in both models. By the tenth trial B has closed part of
      the gap, although in the adaptive model the gap first widens a little. The numerical
      predictions differ, but B starts with more left to learn, and the adaptive model
      also makes it learn less readily. Those influences pull in opposite directions.
      Continuing O1 training mixes the starting-value difference with the difference
      in associability."),
    across = paste0("B ends at ", num(trained$rw$V_B), " in ", RW, " and ",
      num(trained$adaptive$V_B), " in the adaptive model. The models use different
      errors and different learning rates, chosen here to illustrate their behavior.
      B shares the small error left by A in ", RW, "; it learns from its own error in
      the adaptive model. You could compare quantitative predictions with data, but
      these two values alone do not isolate a change in how readily B learns."))
  tells_feedback <- function(ch, verdict) paste0(
    if (verdict == "yes") switch(ch,
      more = "B staying below D would show that blocking persists. It would not distinguish Rescorla–Wagner from the adaptive model. ",
      cont = "Giving B and D the same extra training does not give them the same starting conditions: they already have different values for O1. ",
      across = "This comparison changes more than associability: the error rule and the learning rates also differ between the models. ")
    else "",
    tells_text[[ch]])
  cmp_note <- list(
    more = paste0(RW, ": B ", num(trained$rw$V_B), " and D ", num(trained$rw$V_D), " after ",
      n_base, " compound trials, B ", num(more$rw$V_B), " and D ", num(more$rw$V_D), " after ",
      n_more, ". Adaptive model: B ", num(trained$adaptive$V_B), " and D ",
      num(trained$adaptive$V_D), " after ", n_base, ", B ", num(more$adaptive$V_B), " and D ",
      num(more$adaptive$V_D), " after ", n_more, ". Both leave B below D."),
    cont = paste0("After ten more trials with O1: ", RW, " B ", num(at(co$rw$B$V, 10)), ", D ",
      num(at(co$rw$D$V, 10)), ", gap ", num(at(co$rw$gap, 0)), " at the start and ",
      num(at(co$rw$gap, 10)), " at the end. Adaptive model B ", num(at(co$adaptive$B$V, 10)),
      ", D ", num(at(co$adaptive$D$V, 10)), ", gap ", num(at(co$adaptive$gap, 0)),
      " at the start and ", num(at(co$adaptive$gap, 10)), " at the end."),
    across = paste0("B's learned value ", num(trained$rw$V_B), " (", RW, ") and ",
      num(trained$adaptive$V_B), " (adaptive model). Multipliers on the first compound trial ",
      num(trained$rw$mult_first), " and ", num(trained$adaptive$mult_first), "."),
    new = paste0("Multipliers at the end of compound training: ", RW, " B ",
      num(trained$rw$mult_B), " and D ", num(trained$rw$mult_D), ", adaptive model B ",
      num(trained$adaptive$mult_B), " and D ", num(trained$adaptive$mult_D), "."))
  cmp_settings <- list(
    more = paste0(first_set(phase3 = FALSE), "; also run with ", n_more, " AB+ and ",
                  n_more, " DE+ in Phase 2"),
    cont = paste0(first_set(phase3 = FALSE), "; then ten further B+ and D+ trials with O1,",
                  " starting from the values and associabilities left by Phase 2"),
    across = paste0(first_set(phase3 = FALSE), "; compared at the end of Phase 2"),
    new = first_set())

  cmp_tries <- reactiveVal(list())      # choice, reason and yes/no answer per comparison
  cmp_picking <- reactiveVal(TRUE)      # TRUE while the form for the next comparison is shown
  cmp_msg <- reactiveVal(NULL)

  cmp_try_ui <- function(attempt) {
    ch <- attempt$choice
    div(class = "try",
      div(class = "answered",
        p(span(class = "answered-label", "Comparison"),
          span(class = "answered-choice", cmp_choices[[ch]])),
        if (nzchar(attempt$reason)) p(span(class = "answered-label", "Your reason"),
                                      span(class = "answered-choice", attempt$reason))),
      div(class = "feedback",
        cmp_result[[ch]],
        if (ch == "new") NULL
        else if (is.null(attempt$verdict)) tagList(
          radioButtons(paste0("cmp_tells_", ch), span(class = "item-label", tells_label), inline = TRUE,
                       choiceNames = unname(tells_choices), choiceValues = names(tells_choices),
                       selected = character(0)),
          actionButton(paste0("cmp_check_", ch), "Submit", class = "btn-submit"))
        else tagList(
          p(span(class = "answered-label", tells_label),
            span(class = "answered-choice", tells_choices[[attempt$verdict]])),
          P(tells_feedback(ch, attempt$verdict)))))
  }

  output$cmp <- renderUI({
    tries <- cmp_tries()
    tried <- vapply(tries, `[[`, "", "choice")
    left <- setdiff(names(cmp_choices), tried)
    last <- if (length(tries)) tries[[length(tries)]]
    last_done <- is.null(last) || !is.null(last$verdict)
    n <- length(tries) + 1
    tagList(
      lapply(tries, cmp_try_ui),
      if (cmp_picking() && length(left)) div(class = "try",
        div(class = "item",
          radioButtons(paste0("cmp_choice_", n),
                       span(class = "item-label",
                            if (n == 1) cmp_label else "Which comparison would you try next?"),
                       width = "100%", choiceNames = unname(cmp_choices[left]),
                       choiceValues = left, selected = character(0))),
        textAreaInput(paste0("cmp_reason_", n),
                      "What do you hope to learn from this comparison? A sentence is enough.",
                      rows = 2, width = "100%"),
        actionButton(paste0("cmp_go_", n), "Run it", class = "btn-submit"))
      else if (last_done && length(left) && !("new" %in% tried))
        p(class = "another", actionLink("cmp_another", "Choose another comparison")))
  })
  output$cmp_msg <- renderUI(if (!is.null(cmp_msg())) p(class = "msg", cmp_msg()))

  # Running comparison n. A click counts only while the form for comparison n is
  # open, so a double click runs it once. The new outcome goes to the notes here;
  # the other comparisons go once the reader has said whether they isolate the
  # difference.
  for (i in seq_along(cmp_choices)) local({
    n <- i
    observeEvent(input[[paste0("cmp_go_", n)]], {
      tries <- cmp_tries()
      if (!cmp_picking() || length(tries) != n - 1) return()
      ch <- input[[paste0("cmp_choice_", n)]]
      if (is.null(ch) || !nzchar(ch)) { cmp_msg("Choose a comparison first."); return() }
      reason <- input[[paste0("cmp_reason_", n)]]
      reason <- trimws(if (is.null(reason)) "" else reason)
      if (!nzchar(reason)) {
        cmp_msg("Add a sentence about what you hope to learn before running the comparison.")
        return()
      }
      cmp_msg(NULL)
      cmp_tries(c(tries, list(list(choice = ch, reason = reason, verdict = NULL))))
      cmp_picking(FALSE)
      if (ch == "new") add_note("Step 2", "Comparison chosen", cmp_label,
        paste0(cmp_choices[[ch]], " Reason: ", reason),
        result = cmp_note[[ch]], settings = cmp_settings[[ch]])
    })
  })
  # Answering whether the "more", "cont" or "across" comparison isolates the
  # difference.
  for (choice in c("more", "cont", "across")) local({
    ch <- choice
    observeEvent(input[[paste0("cmp_check_", ch)]], {
      tries <- cmp_tries()
      i <- which(vapply(tries, `[[`, "", "choice") == ch)
      if (!length(i) || !is.null(tries[[i]]$verdict)) return()
      verdict <- input[[paste0("cmp_tells_", ch)]]
      if (is.null(verdict) || !nzchar(verdict)) { cmp_msg("Choose yes or no first."); return() }
      cmp_msg(NULL)
      tries[[i]]$verdict <- verdict
      cmp_tries(tries)
      add_note("Step 2", "Comparison tried", paste0(cmp_choices[[ch]], " ", tells_label),
        paste0(tells_choices[[verdict]], " Reason for choosing it: ", tries[[i]]$reason),
        result = paste0(tells_feedback(ch, verdict), " ", cmp_note[[ch]]),
        settings = cmp_settings[[ch]])
    })
  })
  observeEvent(input$cmp_another, { cmp_msg(NULL); cmp_picking(TRUE) })

  output$p_cont_curves <- renderPlot(plot_curves(co, xlab = "Further trials with O1",
                                                 ylab = "Learned value for O1"))
  output$p_cont_gap <- renderPlot(plot_gap(co, xlab = "Further trials with O1",
                                           ylim = c(-.02, .35)))

  # The prediction for the new outcome, then the result.
  q2_items <- list(
    item("rw", paste0("What gap do you expect under ", RW, "?"), gap_choices),
    item("ad", "What gap do you expect under the adaptive model?", gap_choices),
    item("why", "What would explain a gap under the adaptive model?", c(
      start = "B and D start the new task with different learned values for O2.",
      error = "B and D face different prediction errors on their first O2 trial.",
      assoc = "B and D start with the same value and the same error, but B learns less from that error because its associability is lower.",
      A = "A is still present and uses up part of the prediction error.")))
  first_gains <- paste0("On the first O2 trial both errors are 1, but B gains .3 × ",
    num(at(ad_B$alpha, 0)), " × 1 = ", num(at(ad_B$gain, 0)), " and D gains .3 × ",
    num(at(ad_D$alpha, 0)), " × 1 = ", num(at(ad_D$gain, 0)), ".")
  why_text <- list(
    start = "You attributed the adaptive gap to different starting values. Both cues start at 0 for O2, so the gap starts at zero.",
    error = "You attributed the adaptive gap to different first-trial errors. Both cues start at value 0, so their first errors are equal. Later, B has the larger error, which helps it catch up.",
    assoc = "Equal starting values do give the cues equal errors at first. Their associabilities differ, so they turn that same error into different gains.",
    A = "You attributed the adaptive gap to A's prediction. A is absent during O2 training, and the adaptive model uses each cue's own prediction error.")
  q2_feedback <- function(a) c(
    rw = paste0(switch(a$rw,
      pos = paste0("You expected D to pull ahead under ", RW, ". "),
      neg = paste0("You expected B to pull ahead under ", RW, ". "),
      zero = ""),
      "Under ", RW, ", the gap is zero after every update. Both cues start at 0 for O2
      and train alone with the same fixed update multiplier, so their errors and gains
      stay identical."),
    adaptive = paste0(switch(a$ad,
      zero = "You expected equal learning under the adaptive model. Equal starting values do not reset the cues' associabilities. ",
      neg = "You expected B to pull ahead under the adaptive model. But B starts with lower associability, so it initially gains less from the same error. ",
      pos = ""),
      "D learns faster at first under the adaptive model because its associability
      starts higher than B's.
      The gap grows to ", num(at(base$adaptive$gap, peak_k)), " after ", updates(peak_k),
      " and then narrows to ", num(at(base$adaptive$gap, 10)), " after ten."),
    why = paste0(why_text[[a$why]],
      if (a$why != "assoc") " D's initial advantage comes from associability.",
      " ", first_gains))

  ask_server("q2", input, output, answers, q2_items,
    reason = "Add a thought, if you like", button = "See the learning curves",
    feedback = function(a) {
      tagList(
        lapply(q2_feedback(a), P),
        p("Both models produced blocking, but they predict different learning for O2.
           What if B and D brought some of their old learned values into this task?"))
    },
    on_submit = function(a) add_note("Step 2", "Prediction for the new outcome",
      "B and D learn a new outcome from value 0. What happens to the B–D gap?",
      paste0(RW, ": ", gap_choices[[a$rw]], " Adaptive model: ", gap_choices[[a$ad]],
             " Reason: ", q2_items[[3]]$choices[[a$why]],
             if (nzchar(a$reason)) paste0(" You added: ", a$reason)),
      result = paste(q2_feedback(a), collapse = " "),
      settings = first_set()))

  output$p2_curves <- renderPlot({ req(answers$q2); plot_curves(base) })
  output$p2_gap <- renderPlot({ req(answers$q2); plot_gap(base, ylim = c(-.02, .32)) })

  # One row per step of the calculation, so that the table reads top to bottom.
  output$trial_table <- renderUI({
    req(answers$q2)
    m <- input$t_model; j <- input$t_k
    B <- base[[m]]$B; D <- base[[m]]$D
    row <- function(label, f) tags$tr(tags$td(label), tags$td(f(B)), tags$td(f(D)))
    tagList(tags$table(class = "values",
      tags$thead(tags$tr(tags$th(paste("Update", j)), tags$th(class = "cue-B", "B"),
                         tags$th(class = "cue-D", "D"))),
      tags$tbody(
        row("Value before", function(d) prob(at(d$V, j - 1))),
        row("Error", function(d) prob(at(d$error, j - 1))),
        row("Associability", function(d) if (m == "rw") "—" else num(at(d$alpha, j - 1))),
        row("Multiplier", function(d) num(at(d$mult, j - 1))),
        row("Gain", function(d) num(at(d$gain, j - 1))),
        row("Value after", function(d) num(at(d$V, j))))),
      p(class = "table-note", "Gains, values and gaps are calculated from unrounded values,
        so a hand calculation can differ in the last digit."))
  })
  output$trial_note <- renderUI({
    req(answers$q2)
    m <- input$t_model; j <- input$t_k
    gain_B <- at(base[[m]]$B$gain, j - 1); gain_D <- at(base[[m]]$D$gain, j - 1)
    p(class = "muted", paste0("Gap after update ", j, ": ", prob(at(base[[m]]$gap, j)), ". ",
      if (m == "rw") "B and D gain the same."
      else if (gain_B > gain_D) "On this update B gains more than D, so the gap narrows."
      else "On this update D gains more than B, so the gap grows."))
  })

  q2b_items <- list(item("n", paste0("The adaptive model's gap is largest after ",
      updates(peak_k), " and then narrows. Why?"), c(
    stop = "D stops learning once its value is high enough.",
    converge = "B's associability catches up with D's, so B again learns as readily as D.",
    error = "B has more left to learn, and its larger error comes to outweigh its lower associability, so B starts to gain more per trial than D.",
    overtake = "B's learned value overtakes D's.")))
  alpha_gap <- ad_D$alpha - ad_B$alpha
  narrow_text <- paste0("On update ", peak_k + 1, ", B gains ", num(at(ad_B$gain, peak_k)),
    " and D gains ", num(at(ad_D$gain, peak_k)), ". B is still behind in value but gains
    more on this trial, because it has more left to learn. Its associability is still the
    lower one: D's exceeds B's by ", num(at(alpha_gap, peak_k)), ", up from ",
    num(at(alpha_gap, 0)), " at the start of the new task. B can catch up without overtaking D.")
  ask_server("q2b", input, output, answers, q2b_items,
    feedback = function(a) P(switch(a$n,
      stop = "D keeps learning on every trial. ",
      converge = "B's associability does rise during the new training, but D's rises faster.
                  When a cue is trained alone, a smaller prediction error gives a larger
                  increase in associability. D predicts O2 more accurately than B. ",
      error = "",
      overtake = "B never overtakes D under these assumptions; the gap stays positive
                  after every update. What changes is how much each cue gains per trial. "),
      narrow_text),
    on_submit = function(a) add_note("Step 2", "Why the gap narrows",
      "Why does the adaptive model's gap narrow after its peak?",
      q2b_items[[1]]$choices[[a$n]], result = narrow_text, settings = first_set()))

  # Starting the inquiry again clears the answers and the comparisons tried but
  # keeps the notes.
  list(reset = function() {
    clear_answers(answers, c("q2", "q2b"))
    cmp_tries(list()); cmp_picking(TRUE); cmp_msg(NULL)
  })
}

Participants judge whether a patch of moving dots drifts left or right. In a diffusion model, noisy evidence accumulates until it reaches one of two boundaries. The boundary reached determines the answer; the time taken to reach it is the decision time."), P("You are considering two settings of this model. Drift rate v describes how quickly evidence moves, on average, toward the correct answer. Boundary separation a is the distance between the two boundaries. Evidence starts halfway between them, so wider boundaries require more evidence before an answer. Both settings use the same noise level and have no deadline. The parameters stay fixed across independent trials."), div(class = "scroll-x", tabindex = "0", role = "region", `aria-label` = "The two settings", uiOutput("ddm_table")), ddm_formulas_ui(), p("You have recorded whether each answer was correct, without recording its timing."), div(class = "question", uiOutput("x1")), conditionalPanel("output.done_x1", div(class = "question", uiOutput("x2"))), conditionalPanel("output.done_x2", fig("p_ddm", "300px"), uiOutput("ddm_text"), aside("Section 6."), div(class = "question", uiOutput("x3_prompt"), uiOutput("x3"))), conditionalPanel("output.done_x3", div(class = "end", p("Your notes keep your predictions, the results you saw and your revised conclusions. Download a copy to look back over your reasoning. Reopen an earlier step to review a result, or start again to try different answers."), p(actionLink("restart", "Start the inquiry again"), span(class = "muted", " (your notes are kept)")))) ) decision_server <- function(input, output, answers, add_note) { # The two settings, with their predicted accuracy and mean decision time. dd <- ddm_summary() output$ddm_table <- renderUI(tags$table(class = "values", tags$thead(tags$tr(tags$th(""), tags$th(HTML("Drift rate v")), tags$th(HTML("Boundary separation a")), tags$th("Predicted accuracy"))), tags$tbody( tags$tr(tags$td("First setting"), tags$td(num0(dd$v[1], 2)), tags$td(num0(dd$a[1], 1)), tags$td(num(dd$acc[1]))), tags$tr(tags$td("Second setting"), tags$td(num0(dd$v[2], 2)), tags$td(num0(dd$a[2], 1)), tags$td(num(dd$acc[2])))))) acc_text <- paste0("Accuracy depends on the product of drift rate and boundary separation in this example. That product is 0.60 in both settings, so both predict accuracy ", num(dd$acc[1]), ". Any sequence of correct and incorrect answers is equally likely under the two settings. More trials would estimate accuracy more precisely but would not show which setting produced it.") x1_items <- list(item("more", "Could many more correct-or-incorrect answers tell the two settings apart?", c( yes = "Yes. A larger sample could reveal the effect of the different drift rates.", no = "No. Their predicted accuracies are identical."))) ask_server("x1", input, output, answers, x1_items, feedback = function(a) tagList( if (a$more == "yes") p("You expected more trials to reveal the different drift rates. They cannot, for this reason:"), P(acc_text)), on_submit = function(a) add_note("Step 6", "More accuracy data", x1_items[[1]]$label, x1_items[[1]]$choices[[a$more]], result = acc_text, settings = ddm_settings_text)) x2_items <- list( item("rec", "What else would you record on each trial?", c( rt = "The time from stimulus onset to the participant's response.", conf = "How confident the participant feels.", side = "Which answer was given, left or right.", none = "Nothing else; accuracy is enough.")), item("longer", "Which setting should give the longer decision times?", c( first = "The first (slower drift, wider boundaries).", second = "The second (faster drift, narrower boundaries).", same = "The same for both."))) rt_text <- paste0("Decisions take longer in the first setting. The evidence starts farther from either boundary and moves toward the correct one more slowly. Mean decision time is ", num0(dd$mean[1], 2), ", compared with ", num0(dd$mean[2], 2), " in the second setting, in the model's time units. Noise makes the distributions overlap, but they still differ. Your recorded response times would also include perception and motor execution, called nondecision time. If that extra time is shared between settings, the difference remains. How precisely you could estimate the parameters would still depend on the data available.") ask_server("x2", input, output, answers, x2_items, button = "See the predicted times", feedback = function(a) tagList( if (a$longer == "second") p("You expected longer decisions in the second setting. Its drift is faster and its boundaries are closer; both changes shorten the predicted decision times.") else if (a$longer == "same") p("Equal accuracy does not require equal decision times. The settings differ in both drift and boundary separation."), P(switch(a$rec, rt = "", conf = "You could record confidence, but you would need an additional rule connecting it to the model before comparing predictions. This model already predicts decision times. ", side = "For a given stimulus, both settings predict the same proportions of left and right choices. Recording the chosen side would therefore leave these settings indistinguishable. Their decision times differ. ", none = "With correctness alone you cannot tell these settings apart: both predict the same accuracy, but their decision times differ. "), rt_text)), on_submit = function(a) add_note("Step 6", "What else to record", "What else would you record, and which setting gives the longer decision times?", paste0(x2_items[[1]]$choices[[a$rec]], " ", x2_items[[2]]$choices[[a$longer]]), result = paste0("Mean decision time ", num0(dd$mean[1], 2), " in the first setting and ", num0(dd$mean[2], 2), " in the second; accuracy ", num(dd$acc[1]), " in both."), settings = ddm_settings_text)) output$p_ddm <- renderPlot({ req(answers$x2); plot_ddm(dd) }) output$ddm_text <- renderUI({ req(answers$x2) p(class = "muted", "Both curves are calculated from the model, not simulated. Correct and incorrect responses are pooled, and nondecision time is not included.") }) challenge <- "Now suppose the time needed to perceive the stimulus and make a motor response also differs between settings. If you recorded longer response times under one setting, could you conclude that it had the lower drift rate? What would you want to know before making that claim?" reflection <- "A longer recorded response time need not mean slower evidence accumulation. Wider boundaries or a longer nondecision time could also lengthen it. To draw a conclusion about drift rate, you would need to account for those components and ask whether the combined predictions for choices and response times distinguish your proposed explanations. The two decision-time curves are predictions from two specified settings. A drift rate cannot be read directly from an observed response time." output$x3_prompt <- renderUI(tagList(p(class = "item-label", challenge), p(class = "muted", "Write what you would consider. Save your thoughts to add them to your notes and read the discussion."))) ask_server("x3", input, output, answers, list(), reason = "Your reasoning", reason_required = TRUE, button = "Save my thoughts", feedback = function(a) tagList(h3("Thinking it through"), p(reflection)), on_submit = function(a) add_note("Step 6", "Interpreting response times", challenge, a$reason, result = reflection, settings = paste0(ddm_settings_text, "; decision-time curves exclude nondecision time; ", "challenge allows different nondecision times"))) # Trying another design or case, or starting the inquiry again, clears the # answers but keeps the notes. list(reset = function() clear_answers(answers, c("x1", "x2", "x3"))) }

# Model engine for the companion app
#
# These functions compute every model result the app shows, except the
# simulated experiments of Step 5, which are read from data/inference_cases.rds.
# They call the learning models in models.R (a copy of R/models.R, which the
# scripts for Sections 2 to 4 of the paper use) and add only the bookkeeping the
# app needs: the training design, the carryover assumptions, the changes to the
# adaptive model, the response functions, and the decision-model calculations of
# Step 6.
#
# Checked against the paper's values by tests/verify_app.R.

# From the repository root this is R/models.R; from shiny_app/ it is the copy in
# shiny_app/R/models.R, which the tests require to be identical.
source("R/models.R", local = TRUE)

# The settings of the paper's example.
default_settings <- list(
  rw_alpha = .4, rw_beta = .3,          # Rescorla-Wagner
  S = .3, alpha_init = .5, eta = .05,   # adaptive model
  n_phase1 = 10, n_compound = 10, n_transfer = 10,
  g_V = 0, g_alpha = 1,                 # carryover to the new outcome
  change = "none",                      # none, prevent, remove or supply (Section 4.1)
  e_offset = 0                          # E's salience is S * (1 + e_offset)
)

settings_with <- function(...) modifyList(default_settings, list(...))

# The two-phase training of Section 3.2: A (or C) alone, then A with B (or D
# with E), all with the first outcome O1.
blocking_design <- function(s) c(make_trials("A", 1, s$n_phase1, "Phase 1"),
                                 make_trials(c("A", "B"), 1, s$n_compound, "Phase 2"))
control_design <- function(s) c(make_trials("C", 1, s$n_phase1, "Phase 1"),
                                make_trials(c("D", "E"), 1, s$n_compound, "Phase 2"))


# Phases 1 and 2: what training with O1 leaves behind

trained_states <- function(s = default_settings) {
  blocking <- blocking_design(s)
  control  <- control_design(s)

  rw_b <- rw_final(blocking, alpha = c(A = s$rw_alpha, B = s$rw_alpha), beta = s$rw_beta)
  rw_c <- rw_final(control, alpha = c(C = s$rw_alpha, D = s$rw_alpha, E = s$rw_alpha),
                   beta = s$rw_beta)

  # The adaptive model runs one phase at a time, so that Prevent can hold
  # associability fixed during compound training only (Section 4.1). C's
  # training cannot affect D or E, so the control run starts at Phase 2. The
  # new cues B, D and E start at value zero and associability alpha_init.
  eta_compound <- if (s$change == "prevent") 0 else s$eta
  phase1 <- adaptive_final_state(make_trials("A", 1, s$n_phase1, "Phase 1"),
                                 S = c(A = s$S), alpha_init = c(A = s$alpha_init),
                                 eta = s$eta)
  ad_b <- adaptive_final_state(make_trials(c("A", "B"), 1, s$n_compound, "Phase 2"),
                               S = c(A = s$S, B = s$S),
                               alpha_init = c(A = unname(phase1$alpha), B = s$alpha_init),
                               eta = eta_compound,
                               V_init = c(A = unname(phase1$V), B = 0))
  # A nonzero e_offset makes E slightly more or less salient than D, so that
  # D's error differs slightly from E's (Section 4.5).
  ad_c <- adaptive_final_state(make_trials(c("D", "E"), 1, s$n_compound, "Phase 2"),
                               S = c(D = s$S, E = s$S * (1 + s$e_offset)),
                               alpha_init = c(D = s$alpha_init, E = s$alpha_init),
                               eta = eta_compound,
                               V_init = c(D = 0, E = 0))

  # mult_first is the multiplier on the first compound trial; mult_B and
  # mult_D are the multipliers left at the end of compound training (Table 2).
  list(
    rw = list(V_A = unname(rw_b["A"]), V_B = unname(rw_b["B"]), V_D = unname(rw_c["D"]),
              mult_first = s$rw_alpha * s$rw_beta,
              mult_B = s$rw_alpha * s$rw_beta, mult_D = s$rw_alpha * s$rw_beta),
    adaptive = list(V_A = unname(ad_b$V["A"]), V_B = unname(ad_b$V["B"]),
                    V_D = unname(ad_c$V["D"]),
                    alpha_B = unname(ad_b$alpha["B"]), alpha_D = unname(ad_c$alpha["D"]),
                    mult_first = s$S * s$alpha_init,
                    mult_B = s$S * unname(ad_b$alpha["B"]),
                    mult_D = s$S * unname(ad_c$alpha["D"]))
  )
}

# Compound training trial by trial: what B and D bring into each trial and
# what they gain from it. Rows are the compound trials 1, ..., n_compound. It
# does not apply change or e_offset; the app calls it with the default settings.
compound_trace <- function(s = default_settings) {
  rw_b <- rw_simulate(blocking_design(s), alpha = c(A = s$rw_alpha, B = s$rw_alpha),
                      beta = s$rw_beta)
  rw_c <- rw_simulate(control_design(s), alpha = c(C = s$rw_alpha, D = s$rw_alpha, E = s$rw_alpha),
                      beta = s$rw_beta)
  ad_b <- adaptive_simulate(blocking_design(s), S = c(A = s$S, B = s$S),
                            alpha_init = c(A = s$alpha_init, B = s$alpha_init),
                            eta = s$eta)
  ad_c <- adaptive_simulate(control_design(s), S = c(C = s$S, D = s$S, E = s$S),
                            alpha_init = c(C = s$alpha_init, D = s$alpha_init, E = s$alpha_init),
                            eta = s$eta)
  # The positions of the compound trials in the design. A run holds each cue's
  # state at the start of every trial, so trial t + 1 gives the state after t.
  trials <- s$n_phase1 + seq_len(s$n_compound)
  pick <- function(run, cue, col, t) {
    rows <- run[run$cue == cue, ]
    rows[[col]][match(t, rows$trial)]
  }
  rw <- data.frame(
    trial = seq_len(s$n_compound),
    V_A = pick(rw_b, "A", "V", trials), V_B = pick(rw_b, "B", "V", trials),
    error = 1 - (pick(rw_b, "A", "V", trials) + pick(rw_b, "B", "V", trials)),
    gain_B = pick(rw_b, "B", "V", trials + 1) - pick(rw_b, "B", "V", trials),
    gain_D = pick(rw_c, "D", "V", trials + 1) - pick(rw_c, "D", "V", trials))
  ad <- data.frame(
    trial = seq_len(s$n_compound),
    V_A = pick(ad_b, "A", "V", trials), V_B = pick(ad_b, "B", "V", trials),
    error_A = 1 - pick(ad_b, "A", "V", trials), error_B = 1 - pick(ad_b, "B", "V", trials),
    alpha_B = pick(ad_b, "B", "alpha", trials),
    alpha_B_after = pick(ad_b, "B", "alpha", trials + 1),
    gain_B = pick(ad_b, "B", "V", trials + 1) - pick(ad_b, "B", "V", trials),
    gain_D = pick(ad_c, "D", "V", trials + 1) - pick(ad_c, "D", "V", trials))
  list(rw = rw, adaptive = ad)
}


# Phase 3: each cue learning alone

# One cue trained alone for n_transfer trials, each followed by the outcome,
# under the adaptive model or a fixed-rate learner ("rw"). Given mult, the
# fixed-rate learner uses that multiplier instead of rw_alpha * rw_beta.
# Returns one row per completed update k = 0, ..., n_transfer: V and alpha are
# the values after k updates; error, mult and gain describe update k + 1.
transfer_cue <- function(model, V_start, alpha_start, s, mult = NULL) {
  n <- s$n_transfer
  design <- make_trials("X", 1, n, "Phase 3")
  if (model == "adaptive") {
    run <- adaptive_simulate(design, S = c(X = s$S), alpha_init = c(X = alpha_start),
                             eta = s$eta,
                             V_init = c(X = V_start), cue_names = "X")
    V <- run$V
    alpha <- run$alpha
    multiplier <- s$S * alpha
  } else {
    # One cue under Rescorla-Wagner: the multiplier is passed as its salience,
    # with beta = 1.
    fixed_mult <- if (is.null(mult)) s$rw_alpha * s$rw_beta else mult
    run <- rw_simulate(design, alpha = c(X = fixed_mult), beta = 1,
                       V_init = c(X = V_start), cue_names = "X")
    V <- run$V
    alpha <- rep(NA_real_, n + 1)
    multiplier <- rep(fixed_mult, n + 1)
  }
  data.frame(k = 0:n, V = V, alpha = alpha, mult = multiplier,
             error = c(1 - V[-(n + 1)], NA), gain = c(diff(V), NA))
}

# Both models, both cues, learning the new outcome O2 under the settings in s.
# Each model's gap is the B-D gap, D's value minus B's, after k = 0, ...,
# n_transfer updates (Equation 11).
run_inquiry <- function(s = default_settings) {
  st <- trained_states(s)
  rw <- st$rw
  ad <- st$adaptive

  # Associabilities at the start of O2 (Equation 14). Remove resets both to
  # alpha_init (Section 4.1).
  a_B <- s$alpha_init + s$g_alpha * (ad$alpha_B - s$alpha_init)
  a_D <- s$alpha_init + s$g_alpha * (ad$alpha_D - s$alpha_init)
  if (s$change == "remove") a_B <- a_D <- s$alpha_init

  # Values at the start of O2 are g_V times the final values for O1 (Equation 16).
  rw_B <- transfer_cue("rw", s$g_V * rw$V_B, NA, s)
  rw_D <- transfer_cue("rw", s$g_V * rw$V_D, NA, s)

  if (s$change == "supply") {
    # A fixed-rate learner that starts the new task where the adaptive model
    # starts: the same O2 values and the multipliers S * alpha, which then stay
    # fixed. Each cue is alone, so its error is lambda - V, as in the adaptive
    # model. Only the associability updating differs.
    ad_B <- transfer_cue("rw", s$g_V * ad$V_B, NA, s, mult = s$S * a_B)
    ad_D <- transfer_cue("rw", s$g_V * ad$V_D, NA, s, mult = s$S * a_D)
  } else {
    ad_B <- transfer_cue("adaptive", s$g_V * ad$V_B, a_B, s)
    ad_D <- transfer_cue("adaptive", s$g_V * ad$V_D, a_D, s)
  }

  list(settings = s, trained = st,
       start = list(alpha_B = a_B, alpha_D = a_D),
       rw = list(B = rw_B, D = rw_D, gap = rw_D$V - rw_B$V),
       adaptive = list(B = ad_B, D = ad_D, gap = ad_D$V - ad_B$V))
}

# Both models, both cues, when training continues with the first outcome O1
# (Step 2): each cue alone, starting from the values and associabilities that
# compound training left. Returns the same structure as run_inquiry().
continue_o1 <- function(s = default_settings) {
  st <- trained_states(s)
  rw <- st$rw
  ad <- st$adaptive
  rw_B <- transfer_cue("rw", rw$V_B, NA, s)
  rw_D <- transfer_cue("rw", rw$V_D, NA, s)
  ad_B <- transfer_cue("adaptive", ad$V_B, ad$alpha_B, s)
  ad_D <- transfer_cue("adaptive", ad$V_D, ad$alpha_D, s)
  list(settings = s, trained = st,
       start = list(alpha_B = ad$alpha_B, alpha_D = ad$alpha_D),
       rw = list(B = rw_B, D = rw_D, gap = rw_D$V - rw_B$V),
       adaptive = list(B = ad_B, D = ad_D, gap = ad_D$V - ad_B$V))
}

# The gap after k updates as old-value carryover varies (Figure 7a).
gap_by_value_carryover <- function(k = 8, g_V = seq(0, 1, by = .01),
                                   s = default_settings) {
  rows <- lapply(g_V, function(g) {
    r <- run_inquiry(modifyList(s, list(g_V = g)))
    c(g_V = g, rw = r$rw$gap[k + 1], adaptive = r$adaptive$gap[k + 1])
  })
  as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, rows))
}


# From learned value to a yes response: the response functions of Section 2.5,
# with the slope and midpoint of Section 4.4

response_prob <- function(V, rule = c("sigmoid", "threshold"),
                          gamma = 8, theta = .5) {
  rule <- match.arg(rule)
  if (rule == "sigmoid") obs_sigmoid(V, gamma = gamma, theta = theta)
  else obs_threshold(V, theta = theta)
}


# The decision model of Step 6
#
# A drift diffusion model with noise scale 1, boundaries at 0 and a, start at
# a/2, and no deadline. The accuracy and the mean decision time have closed
# forms; the decision-time density uses the large-time series of Navarro and
# Fuss (2009), as in the paper's Figure 12.

ddm_settings <- data.frame(id = c("first", "second"), v = c(.30, .60), a = c(2.0, 1.0))

ddm_acc <- function(v, a) 1 / (1 + exp(-v * a))                  # Equation 22
ddm_mean <- function(v, a) a / (2 * v) * tanh(v * a / 2)         # mean decision time
# Density at the lower boundary, with the start at w * a and K terms of the series.
ddm_dens_lower <- function(t, v, a, w = .5, K = 300) {
  k <- seq_len(K)
  sapply(t, function(tt) {
    if (tt <= 0) return(0)
    (pi / a^2) * exp(-v * a * w - v^2 * tt / 2) *
      sum(k * exp(-k^2 * pi^2 * tt / (2 * a^2)) * sin(k * pi * w))
  })
}
# Both boundaries together: the upper boundary (the correct response) uses -v
# and 1 - w, which is also .5.
ddm_dens <- function(t, v, a) ddm_dens_lower(t, v, a) + ddm_dens_lower(t, -v, a)

ddm_summary <- function() {
  d <- ddm_settings
  d$acc <- ddm_acc(d$v, d$a)
  d$mean <- ddm_mean(d$v, d$a)
  d
}

# Explore: change the settings freely
# The controls cover the changes to the adaptive model (Section 4.1), training
# and the associability-change rate (4.2), carryover to O2 (4.3), the response
# rule (4.4) and the salience of the control cue E (4.5). Every curve is computed
# live with engine.R.

explore_ui <- function() div(class = "part wide",
  p(class = "lead",
    "Try changing the training, what carries over to O2, or the response function.
     The curves update as you go. You start with the settings used in the inquiry
     and the tutorial."),
  p(class = "muted", "B is trained together with A, which already predicts the
     training outcome O1; D is trained together with the new cue E and serves as B's
     control. O2 is the new outcome. A positive B–D gap means D's learned value is
     higher than B's."),
  p(class = "muted", "The saved cases in Step 5 stay the same, and Explore settings
     are not added to your inquiry notes."),
  div(class = "explore",
    div(class = "explore-controls",
      div(class = "control-primary",
        h3("Change the adaptive model"),
        p(class = "muted", "In the adaptive model, associability controls how much a cue
           learns from its prediction error: the outcome minus the cue's value.
           The update multiplier is salience (a fixed cue weight) × associability.
           Multiply the error by this multiplier to get the value update."),
        radioButtons("x_change", span(class = "visually-hidden", "Change the adaptive model"), choices = c(
          "No change: keep the adaptive model" = "none",
          "Prevent: keep associability fixed during compound training" = "prevent",
          "Remove: reset associability before O2" = "remove",
          "Supply: use fixed update multipliers during O2" = "supply")),
        uiOutput("x_change_hint"),
        p(class = "small-screen-note", tags$a(href = "#x_change_explanation", "Read about this change")),
        aside("Section 4.1 compares these changes with no old-value carryover (Figure 5).")),
      tags$details(class = "control-group", open = NA, `data-mobile-collapse` = "true",
        tags$summary("Training"),
        p(class = "muted", "Set how many times AB and DE are each presented together,
           followed by O1. Earlier A and C training stays at ten trials each.
           The change rate controls how strongly associability responds to the
           difference between prediction errors throughout O1 and O2, wherever the
           selected model allows it to change."),
        sliderInput("x_n2", "Compound trials per pair", 1, 30, 10, step = 1, ticks = FALSE),
        sliderInput("x_eta", HTML("Associability-change rate, η"), .01, .10, .05,
                    step = .01, ticks = FALSE)),
      tags$details(class = "control-group", open = NA, `data-mobile-collapse` = "true",
        tags$summary("Carryover to O2"),
        p(class = "muted", "For old value, 0 starts both cues at zero; 1 keeps each
           cue's final O1 value. For associability, 0 resets each cue to .5;
           1 keeps its final O1 associability. Half carryover keeps half the old value,
           or half the associability change from .5; it does not halve associability itself."),
        sliderInput("x_gv", HTML(paste0("Old value, ", gV)), 0, 1, 0, step = .05,
                    ticks = FALSE),
        sliderInput("x_ga", HTML(paste0("Associability, ", gA)), 0, 1, 1, step = .05,
                    ticks = FALSE)),
      tags$details(class = "control-group", id = "control-e",
        tags$summary("Control cue E"),
        p(class = "muted", "Salience is a cue's fixed weight in learning. These settings
           change E's weight slightly while keeping D's fixed."),
        p(class = "muted", "Under this rule, a tiny error difference produces a tiny
           associability change, so the curves and rounded table values may look the
           same. Step 3's control-cue exercise and the tutorial's Section 4.5 explain
           this result."),
        radioButtons("x_e", span(class = "visually-hidden", "Control cue E: salience relative to D"), choices = c(
          "Same salience as D" = "0",
          "One part in a million more salient than D" = "1e-6",
          "One part in a million less salient than D" = "-1e-6"))),
      tags$details(class = "control-group",
        tags$summary("Response function"),
        p(class = "muted", "These settings affect only the response plot. The sigmoid
           rises smoothly; its midpoint gives a yes probability of .5, and a
           larger slope makes the rise steeper. The threshold rule gives yes only
           above the threshold. Both cues use the same rule."),
        radioButtons("x_rule", span(class = "visually-hidden", "Response function"), inline = TRUE,
                     choices = c("Sigmoid" = "sigmoid", "Threshold" = "threshold")),
        conditionalPanel("input.x_rule == 'sigmoid'",
          sliderInput("x_gamma", HTML("Slope, γ"), 1, 16, 8, step = .5, ticks = FALSE)),
        sliderInput("x_theta", HTML("Midpoint or threshold, θ"), 0, 1, .5, step = .05,
                    ticks = FALSE)),
      actionLink("x_reset", "Reset these settings")),
    div(class = "explore-output",
      uiOutput("x_change_explanation"),
      tags$details(class = "starting-states", id = "x_starting_states",
        tags$summary("Check the values and update multipliers"),
        uiOutput("x_summary")),
      fig("x_curves", "300px"),
      fig("x_gap", "280px"),
      fig("x_resp", "280px"),
      h3("Update by update"),
      uiOutput("x_table_note"),
      div(class = "scroll-x", tabindex = "0", role = "region",
          `aria-label` = "Values after each O2 update", uiOutput("x_table"))))
)


explore_server <- function(input, output, session) {
  x_run <- reactive({
    req(input$x_n2, input$x_eta, !is.null(input$x_gv), !is.null(input$x_ga), input$x_change)
    run_inquiry(settings_with(
      n_compound = input$x_n2, eta = input$x_eta, g_V = input$x_gv,
      g_alpha = input$x_ga, change = input$x_change,
      e_offset = if (is.null(input$x_e)) 0 else as.numeric(input$x_e)))
  })
  x_label <- reactive(if (input$x_change == "supply") "Fixed-rate learner" else "Adaptive model")
  x_gamma <- reactive(if (is.null(input$x_gamma)) 8 else input$x_gamma)

  output$x_change_hint <- renderUI({
    req(input$x_change)
    p(class = "muted", switch(input$x_change,
      none = "Associability can change during O1 and O2 learning.",
      prevent = "Associability is held fixed during compound training only.",
      remove = "Both associabilities restart at .5 when O2 begins.",
      supply = "Each cue keeps its own starting update multiplier throughout O2. Its learned value still changes."))
  })
  output$x_change_explanation <- renderUI({
    req(input$x_change)
    div(class = "model-change-explanation",
      switch(input$x_change,
        none = tagList(
          h3("The unchanged adaptive model"),
          p("During compound training, each cue's associability rises when it predicts
             the outcome better than the cue presented with it and falls when it predicts
             worse, by an amount that grows with the difference between their errors. The
             carryover sliders set the values and associabilities that each cue brings to O2,
             where associability can change again."),
          p("Use these curves as a reference when you try one of the changes.
             For a cue learning alone, its error is compared with the error of
             predicting zero; associability can rise as the cue learns.")),
        prevent = tagList(
          h3("Prevent: keep associability fixed during compound training"),
          p("Keep each cue's associability at the value it had just before AB and DE
             training. B and D both start that phase at .5, so B cannot acquire a lower
             associability than D during those trials. Their values for O1 still change.
             Associability can change again once O2 training begins."),
          p("Does B's later disadvantage depend on an associability difference
             developing during compound training?"),
          p(class = "muted", "This also changes what B learns about O1. If you allow
             old-value carryover, the difference in O1 learning affects its starting
             value for O2. The associability-carryover slider makes no difference to
             B and D here, because both leave compound training at baseline.")),
        remove = tagList(
          h3("Remove: reset associability when O2 begins"),
          p("Run O1 training as usual, then reset B's and D's associabilities to .5
             just before their first O2 trial. Their learned O1 values stay intact,
             and the old-value carryover slider still sets how much of those values
             enters O2. Associability can change again during O2 learning."),
          p("Does B's later disadvantage depend on retaining the associability
             difference from O1? Here you remove that difference after it has formed
             and keep the earlier value learning."),
          p(class = "muted", "While Remove is selected, the associability-carryover
             slider has no effect: both cues restart at .5.
             Prevent changes O1 learning; Remove changes associability only when O2
             begins. With old-value carryover, B therefore starts O2 at a different value
             under the two changes.")),
        supply = {
          r <- x_run()
          tagList(
            h3("Supply: start a fixed-rate learner where the adaptive model starts"),
            p("Give each cue the O2 starting value and update multiplier it would
               have in the unchanged adaptive model, using your current carryover
               settings. Keep each multiplier fixed throughout O2. The learner still
               updates its values from prediction error on every trial."),
            P("B's fixed multiplier is ", num(at(r$adaptive$B$mult, 0)),
              "; D's is ", num(at(r$adaptive$D$mult, 0)), ". These are taken from
               the adaptive model's salience × associability at the start of O2.
               The separate ", RW, " curve keeps its own starting values and rate."),
            p("How much of the B–D gap comes from the starting values and multipliers,
               and how much depends on associability continuing to change during O2?"))
        }),
      if (input$x_change != "none") p(class = "muted", "In the gap plot, the pale line
        labeled “No change” shows the unchanged adaptive model with the same slider settings."))
  })

  output$x_summary <- renderUI({
    r <- x_run(); end_o1 <- r$trained$adaptive
    row <- function(label, B, D) tags$tr(tags$td(label), tags$td(prob(B)), tags$td(prob(D)))
    tagList(
      p("The O1 rows show the adaptive model at the end of training. The O2 rows
         show the starting states used for the second panel of curves."),
      div(class = "scroll-x", tabindex = "0", role = "region",
          `aria-label` = "Starting states", tags$table(class = "values",
        tags$thead(tags$tr(tags$th(""), tags$th(class = "cue-B", "B"), tags$th(class = "cue-D", "D"))),
        tags$tbody(
          row("Value at the end of O1", end_o1$V_B, end_o1$V_D),
          row("Associability at the end of O1", end_o1$alpha_B, end_o1$alpha_D),
          row("Value at the start of O2", at(r$adaptive$B$V, 0), at(r$adaptive$D$V, 0)),

        prob(at(r$rw$D$V, 0)), " (D), with multiplier ", num(at(r$rw$B$mult, 0)),

  })
  # Drawn even while its details are closed, because the Explore link of Step 3
  # waits for it before scrolling to the results (app.R).
  outputOptions(output, "x_summary", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)
  output$x_curves <- renderPlot(plot_curves(x_run(),
    labels = c(rw = "Rescorla–Wagner", adaptive = x_label())))
  # The unchanged adaptive model, drawn for reference when a change is selected.
  x_ref <- reactive(if (input$x_change == "none") NULL else
    run_inquiry(modifyList(x_run()$settings, list(change = "none"))))
  # The axis always spans at least -.02 to .25, so a small gap looks small.

             ylim = range(-.02, .25, r$rw$gap, r$adaptive$gap, x_ref()$adaptive$gap))

    if (input$x_change == "supply") "The last two columns show the fixed update
      multiplier for each cue. These multipliers stay constant while the learned
      values change."
    else "Follow each cue's O2 value and associability after every update."))

    cues <- function() list(tags$th(class = "cue-B", "B"), tags$th(class = "cue-D", "D"))
    tags$table(class = "values grouped",
      tags$thead(
        tags$tr(tags$th(""), tags$th(colspan = 2, span(HTML(RW))),

      tags$tbody(lapply(1:10, function(k) tags$tr(tags$td(k),
        tags$td(num(at(r$rw$B$V, k))), tags$td(num(at(r$rw$D$V, k))),
        tags$td(num(at(r$adaptive$B$V, k))), tags$td(num(at(r$adaptive$D$V, k))),
        tags$td(num(at(r$adaptive$B[[third]], k))), tags$td(num(at(r$adaptive$D[[third]], k)))))))
  })

  explore_defaults <- function() {
    updateSliderInput(session, "x_n2", value = 10)
    updateSliderInput(session, "x_eta", value = .05)
    updateSliderInput(session, "x_gv", value = 0)
    updateSliderInput(session, "x_ga", value = 1)
    updateRadioButtons(session, "x_change", selected = "none")
    updateRadioButtons(session, "x_e", selected = "0")
    updateRadioButtons(session, "x_rule", selected = "sigmoid")
    updateSliderInput(session, "x_gamma", value = 8)
    updateSliderInput(session, "x_theta", value = .5)
  }
  observeEvent(input$x_reset, explore_defaults())
  list(defaults = explore_defaults)
}
