# Learning models of Sections 2-4: Rescorla-Wagner (Equation 1), the adaptive
# model (Equations 7 and 8) and the response rules of Section 2.5. Base R only.
# The analyses, tests/verify_models.R, the reference implementation in
# R/inference.R and the companion app use these functions.
#
# A design is a list of trials made by make_trials(). Each trial gives the cues
# present ($cues), the outcome lambda ($lambda, 1 or 0) and a phase label
# ($phase).


# Rescorla-Wagner model (Equation 1). The cues present on a trial share one
# prediction error, lambda minus their summed value; absent cues keep their
# values, and the saliences alpha and the rate beta do not change with
# training. Returns one row per cue and trial, holding the value at the start
# of the trial; trial length(design) + 1 holds the values after the last trial.
rw_simulate <- function(design, alpha, beta, V_init = NULL, cue_names = NULL) {
  if (is.null(cue_names))
    cue_names <- unique(unlist(lapply(design, function(x) x$cues)))
  n_cues   <- length(cue_names)
  n_trials <- length(design)

  if (!all(cue_names %in% names(alpha)))
    stop("alpha must contain named values for all cues: ", paste(cue_names, collapse = ", "))

  V <- if (is.null(V_init)) setNames(rep(0, n_cues), cue_names) else V_init
  # Column t holds the values at the start of trial t.
  V_by_trial <- matrix(NA_real_, n_cues, n_trials + 1)
  V_by_trial[, 1] <- V[cue_names]

  for (t in seq_along(design)) {
    cues_present <- design[[t]]$cues
    lambda       <- design[[t]]$lambda

    # The error is computed before any value changes, so cues presented
    # together receive the same error (Section 2.2).
    delta <- lambda - sum(V[cues_present])
    V[cues_present] <- V[cues_present] + alpha[cues_present] * beta * delta

    V_by_trial[, t + 1] <- V[cue_names]
  }

  phases <- vapply(design, function(x) x$phase, character(1))
  data.frame(
    trial = rep(seq_len(n_trials + 1), each = n_cues),
    phase = rep(c(phases, phases[n_trials]), each = n_cues),
    cue   = rep(cue_names, n_trials + 1),
    V     = as.vector(V_by_trial),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}


# Adaptive model (Equations 7 and 8). Each cue present learns from its own
# error, lambda - V_i, scaled by its salience S_i and its associability
# alpha_i. Associability changes by eta times the other cue's absolute error
# minus the cue's own, so it rises when the cue predicts more accurately than
# the other cue, falls when it predicts less accurately, and stays unchanged
# when the errors are equal. A cue presented alone is compared with the error
# of predicting zero, |lambda|. Absent cues keep their values and
# associabilities.
#
# alpha_init and V_init give the state at the start of the run: alpha_init
# and zero before training, or alpha_i(0) (Equation 14) and V_i,O2(0)
# (Equation 16) for a run with the new outcome. Equation 8 keeps associability
# within [alpha_min, alpha_max] = [.01, 1]. Returns one row per cue and trial,
# holding V and alpha at the start of the trial; trial length(design) + 1
# holds the values after the last trial.
adaptive_simulate <- function(design, S, alpha_init,
                              eta = 0.05,
                              V_init = NULL, cue_names = NULL,
                              alpha_min = 0.01, alpha_max = 1.0) {
  if (is.null(cue_names))
    cue_names <- unique(unlist(lapply(design, function(x) x$cues)))
  n_cues   <- length(cue_names)
  n_trials <- length(design)

  if (!all(cue_names %in% names(S)) || !all(cue_names %in% names(alpha_init)))
    stop("S and alpha_init must contain named values for all cues: ",
         paste(cue_names, collapse = ", "))

  V <- if (is.null(V_init)) setNames(rep(0, n_cues), cue_names) else V_init
  alpha <- alpha_init
  # Column t holds the values and associabilities at the start of trial t.
  V_by_trial <- alpha_by_trial <- matrix(NA_real_, n_cues, n_trials + 1)
  V_by_trial[, 1] <- V[cue_names]
  alpha_by_trial[, 1] <- alpha[cue_names]

  for (t in seq_along(design)) {
    cues_present <- design[[t]]$cues
    lambda       <- design[[t]]$lambda

    # Both the value update and the error comparison use the values at the
    # start of the trial, so a change in associability takes effect on the
    # next trial (Section 3.1).
    V_start <- V

    for (cue in cues_present) {
      V[cue] <- V[cue] + S[cue] * alpha[cue] * (lambda - V[cue])
    }

    # e_own and e_other are e_i and e_-i of Equation 8. With more than two
    # cues present, which the paper does not use, e_other is the error of the
    # other cues' summed prediction.
    for (cue in cues_present) {
      others  <- setdiff(cues_present, cue)
      e_own   <- abs(lambda - V_start[cue])
      e_other <- if (length(others) > 0) {
        abs(lambda - sum(V_start[others]))
      } else {
        abs(lambda)
      }

      alpha[cue] <- max(alpha_min, min(alpha_max, alpha[cue] + eta * (e_other - e_own)))
    }

    V_by_trial[, t + 1] <- V[cue_names]
    alpha_by_trial[, t + 1] <- alpha[cue_names]
  }

  phases <- vapply(design, function(x) x$phase, character(1))
  data.frame(
    trial = rep(seq_len(n_trials + 1), each = n_cues),
    phase = rep(c(phases, phases[n_trials]), each = n_cues),
    cue   = rep(cue_names, n_trials + 1),
    V     = as.vector(V_by_trial),
    alpha = as.vector(alpha_by_trial),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}


# The same two models, returning only the state after the last trial: the
# values, and for the adaptive model also the associabilities. They are
# written separately from rw_simulate() and adaptive_simulate() so that
# tests/verify_models.R can compare the two versions, as described in
# Section 2.2. The loop in rw_final() is the one printed there.
rw_final <- function(design, alpha, beta, V_init = NULL) {
  cue_names <- unique(unlist(lapply(design, function(x) x$cues)))
  V <- if (is.null(V_init)) setNames(rep(0, length(cue_names)), cue_names) else V_init
  for (t in seq_along(design)) {
    cues <- design[[t]]$cues
    delta <- design[[t]]$lambda - sum(V[cues])
    V[cues] <- V[cues] + alpha[cues] * beta * delta
  }
  V
}

adaptive_final_state <- function(design, S, alpha_init,
                                 eta = 0.05,
                                 V_init = NULL,
                                 alpha_min = 0.01, alpha_max = 1.0) {
  cue_names <- unique(unlist(lapply(design, function(x) x$cues)))
  V <- if (is.null(V_init)) setNames(rep(0, length(cue_names)), cue_names) else V_init
  alpha <- alpha_init
  for (t in seq_along(design)) {
    cues    <- design[[t]]$cues
    lambda  <- design[[t]]$lambda
    V_start <- V
    for (cue in cues) {
      V[cue] <- V[cue] + S[cue] * alpha[cue] * (lambda - V[cue])
    }
    for (cue in cues) {
      others  <- setdiff(cues, cue)
      e_own   <- abs(lambda - V_start[cue])
      e_other <- if (length(others) > 0) abs(lambda - sum(V_start[others])) else abs(lambda)
      alpha[cue] <- max(alpha_min, min(alpha_max, alpha[cue] + eta * (e_other - e_own)))
    }
  }
  list(V = V, alpha = alpha)
}


# n identical trials: the cues present, the outcome lambda and a phase label.
make_trials <- function(cues, lambda, n, phase_label) {
  lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
    list(cues = cues, lambda = lambda, phase = phase_label)
  })
}

# Values and associabilities after the last trial of a run of rw_simulate()
# or adaptive_simulate().
extract_final_V <- function(run) {
  final <- run[run$trial == max(run$trial), ]
  setNames(final$V, final$cue)
}

extract_final_alpha <- function(run) {
  final <- run[run$trial == max(run$trial), ]
  setNames(final$alpha, final$cue)
}


# Response rules of Section 2.5, which turn a learned value V into the
# probability of a response: the sigmoid of Equation 5, with slope gamma and
# midpoint theta, and the threshold rule of Equation 6.
obs_sigmoid <- function(V, gamma = 5, theta = 0.5) {
  1 / (1 + exp(-gamma * (V - theta)))
}

obs_threshold <- function(V, theta = 0.5) {
  as.numeric(V > theta)
}


# Prints the first n_trace trials of a Rescorla-Wagner run step by step, so
# that the shared error on a compound trial can be checked by hand
# (Section 2.2). Returns the values after those trials.
rw_hand_trace <- function(design, alpha, beta, n_trace = 5) {
  cue_names <- unique(unlist(lapply(design, function(x) x$cues)))
  V <- setNames(rep(0, length(cue_names)), cue_names)
  # Numbers as Section 2.3 writes them, without a leading zero.
  fmt <- function(x, digits = 4) sub("^(-?)0\\.", "\\1.", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits))

  for (t in seq_len(min(n_trace, length(design)))) {
    cues   <- design[[t]]$cues
    lambda <- design[[t]]$lambda
    phase  <- design[[t]]$phase
    sum_V  <- sum(V[cues])
    delta  <- lambda - sum_V

    cat(sprintf("Trial %d [%s]: cues = {%s}, lambda = %g\n",
                t, phase, paste(cues, collapse = ", "), lambda))
    cat(sprintf("  V before: %s\n",
                paste(sprintf("%s = %s", cue_names, fmt(V[cue_names])), collapse = ", ")))
    cat(sprintf("  delta = lambda - sum of V present = %g - %s = %s\n",
                lambda, fmt(sum_V), fmt(delta)))
    for (cue in cues) {
      cat(sprintf("  change in V_%s = alpha_%s * beta * delta = %s * %s * %s = %s\n",
                  cue, cue, fmt(alpha[cue], 2), fmt(beta, 2), fmt(delta),
                  fmt(alpha[cue] * beta * delta)))
    }

    V[cues] <- V[cues] + alpha[cues] * beta * delta

    cat(sprintf("  V after:  %s\n\n",
                paste(sprintf("%s = %s", cue_names, fmt(V[cue_names])), collapse = ", ")))
  }
  invisible(V)
}

# The opening: why did participants learn so little about the light?
# opening_ui() introduces blocking and the two explanations that the inquiry
# compares, and lays out the buttons for the six steps.

opening_ui <- function() tagList(
  h2(class = "opening", "Why did participants learn so little about the light?"),
  p("Participants have learned that a tone means food is coming. You now add a light:
     tone and light appear together, followed by food. After several trials, you present
     the light on its own and ask whether they expect food. Few say yes, even though
     the light has accompanied food every time. Had the tone been new as well, many
     more would say yes to the light. This is called blocking."),
  p(class = "muted", "The tone and light are cues; the food is the outcome.
     Prediction error is the difference between the outcome and what was expected."),
  p("Perhaps the tone already predicts the food so well that there is little
     prediction error left for the light. Or perhaps training changes how readily the
     participants learn about the light. Both explanations can account for blocking.
     What could you try next to find out where their predictions differ?"),
  tags$details(tags$summary("The two learning models"),
    tags$ul(
      tags$li(HTML(paste0("The ", RW, " model updates each cue's learned value using
        the prediction error shared by all cues present. The well-trained tone leaves
        little error for the new light to learn from."))),
      tags$li(HTML("The adaptive-associability model changes how readily participants
        learn about each cue. It lowers the light's associability when the light
        predicts the food less accurately than the tone does. Lower associability
        means a smaller value update for the same prediction error. Associability
        represents attention in this explanation; attention is not measured directly.")))),
  p("Start with what the two models say happened during training. Then choose a
     follow-up comparison and see whether its results change your view."),
  p(class = "muted", "You can work through the six steps without reading the tutorial.

# Plots for the companion app

library(ggplot2)

# The colors of the paper's figures (R/figure_style.R), repeated here because
# shiny_app/ is self-contained. B is red and D blue.
ink   <- "#252525"
grey  <- "#696969"
light <- "#BFBFBF"
col_B <- "#B64B41"
col_D <- "#35658D"

theme_app <- function(base_size = 13) {
  theme_classic(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      text = element_text(colour = ink),
      axis.text = element_text(colour = ink, size = base_size - 2),
      axis.line = element_line(linewidth = .3, colour = ink),
      axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = .3, colour = ink),
      plot.title = element_text(size = base_size, face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 4)),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = base_size - 2, colour = grey, margin = margin(b = 8)),
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      strip.background = element_blank(),
      strip.text = element_text(size = base_size - 1, face = "bold", hjust = 0),
      strip.clip = "off",
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.margin = margin(8, 14, 8, 8)
    )
}

# Positions for the labels at the ends of the lines: at least min_gap apart, in
# the order of y, with the same mean as y.
spread_labels <- function(y, min_gap) {
  o <- order(y)
  s <- y[o]
  for (i in seq_along(s)[-1]) s[i] <- max(s[i], s[i - 1] + min_gap)
  y[o] <- s - (mean(s) - mean(y[o]))
  y
}

# A zero line that stops at the last update, so that it does not run through
# the end labels.
zero_line <- function(k_max)
  annotate("segment", x = -Inf, xend = k_max, y = 0, yend = 0, colour = light, linewidth = .3)


# B and D learning curves, one panel per model, as in Figure 4b and c.
plot_curves <- function(r, labels = c(rw = "Rescorla–Wagner", adaptive = "Adaptive model"),
                        xlab = "Completed updates with O2", ylab = "Learned value for O2") {
  models <- c("rw", "adaptive")
  d <- do.call(rbind, lapply(models, function(m) rbind(
    data.frame(model = labels[[m]], cue = "B", k = r[[m]]$B$k, V = r[[m]]$B$V),
    data.frame(model = labels[[m]], cue = "D", k = r[[m]]$D$k, V = r[[m]]$D$V))))
  d$model <- factor(d$model, levels = unname(labels[models]))
  # When B and D coincide, draw D dashed over B and label the pair once.
  same <- vapply(models, function(m) max(abs(r[[m]]$B$V - r[[m]]$D$V)) < 1e-12, logical(1))
  same_labels <- unname(labels[models][same])
  d$dash <- d$cue == "D" & d$model %in% same_labels
  ends <- d[d$k == max(d$k) & !(d$cue == "B" & d$model %in% same_labels), ]
  ends$label <- ifelse(ends$model %in% same_labels, "B, D", ends$cue)
  ends$col <- ifelse(ends$model %in% same_labels, ink, c(B = col_B, D = col_D)[ends$cue])
  ends$y <- ave(ends$V, ends$model, FUN = function(v) spread_labels(v, .07))
  ggplot(d, aes(k, V, colour = cue)) +
    geom_line(aes(linetype = dash), linewidth = .8) +
    geom_point(size = 1.6) +
    geom_text(data = ends, aes(y = y, label = label), colour = ends$col, hjust = -.25,
              size = 4.2, fontface = "bold") +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "solid", `TRUE` = "22")) +
    facet_wrap(~model, nrow = 1) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(B = col_B, D = col_D)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 5, 10), expand = expansion(mult = c(.02, .16))) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, .5, 1), labels = c("0", ".5", "1")) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1), clip = "off") +   # end labels may run past the panel
    labs(x = xlab, y = ylab) +
    theme_app() +
    theme(panel.spacing.x = unit(1.6, "lines"))
}

# The B-D gap, D minus B, for both models, as in Figure 4d. "ref" adds the
# unchanged adaptive model as a light line, for comparison with a changed one.
plot_gap <- function(r, title = "The B–D gap (D minus B)", ylim = NULL,
                     second = "Adaptive model", ref = NULL, ref_label = "No change",
                     xlab = "Completed updates with O2") {
  d <- rbind(data.frame(model = "Rescorla–Wagner", k = r$rw$B$k, gap = r$rw$gap),
             data.frame(model = second, k = r$adaptive$B$k, gap = r$adaptive$gap))
  d$model <- factor(d$model, levels = c("Rescorla–Wagner", second))
  ends <- data.frame(label = c("Rescorla–Wagner", second), gap = d$gap[d$k == max(d$k)],
                     col = c(grey, ink))
  if (!is.null(ref)) {
    ref_gap <- data.frame(k = ref$adaptive$B$k, gap = ref$adaptive$gap)
    ends <- rbind(ends, data.frame(label = ref_label, gap = ref_gap$gap[nrow(ref_gap)],
                                   col = grey))
  }
  y_range <- if (is.null(ylim)) range(d$gap, ends$gap, 0) else ylim
  ends$y <- spread_labels(ends$gap, .075 * diff(y_range))
  ends$k <- max(d$k)
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(k, gap)) + zero_line(max(d$k))
  if (!is.null(ref)) p <- p + geom_line(data = ref_gap, colour = light, linewidth = .8)
  p +
    geom_line(aes(linetype = model, colour = model), linewidth = .8) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = model), size = 1.6) +
    geom_text(data = ends, aes(k, y, label = label), colour = ends$col, hjust = 0,
              nudge_x = .3, size = 3.8) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(c(grey, ink), c("Rescorla–Wagner", second))) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = setNames(c("22", "solid"), c("Rescorla–Wagner", second))) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 5, 10), expand = expansion(mult = c(.02, .02))) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = axis_num) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 15.5), ylim = ylim, clip = "off") +
    labs(x = xlab, y = "Gap in learned value", title = title) +
    theme_app()
}

# Gap after eight updates as old-value carryover varies (Figure 7a). As in that
# figure, an open circle marks the adaptive model's original setting, g_V = 0.
plot_gap_by_gV <- function(grid, g_now, cross = NULL) {
  d <- rbind(data.frame(model = "Rescorla–Wagner", g_V = grid$g_V, gap = grid$rw),
             data.frame(model = "Adaptive model", g_V = grid$g_V, gap = grid$adaptive))
  origin <- d$model == "Adaptive model" & d$g_V == 0
  now <- d[abs(d$g_V - g_now) < 1e-9, ]
  ends <- d[d$g_V == max(d$g_V), ]
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(g_V, gap, colour = model, linetype = model)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = .8) +
    geom_point(data = d[origin, ], shape = 21, fill = "white", size = 2.6, stroke = .8) +
    geom_point(data = now, size = 3) +
    geom_text(data = ends, aes(label = model), hjust = 0, nudge_x = .02, size = 3.8) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("Rescorla–Wagner" = grey, "Adaptive model" = ink)) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c("Rescorla–Wagner" = "22", "Adaptive model" = "solid")) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, .5, 1), labels = c("0", ".5", "1")) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = axis_num) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1.45), ylim = c(0, .32), clip = "off") +
    labs(x = expression("Old-value carryover, " * italic(g)[V]),
         y = "Gap after eight updates",
         title = "Changing old-value carryover") +
    theme_app() +
    theme(plot.margin = margin(8, 24, 8, 8))
  if (!is.null(cross)) p <- p +
    annotate("segment", x = cross, xend = cross, y = 0,
             yend = grid$rw[which.min(abs(grid$g_V - cross))], colour = light, linewidth = .4) +
    annotate("text", x = cross, y = .02, label = paste("equal gaps at", num(cross)),
             hjust = -.06, size = 3.5, colour = grey)
  p
}

# Step 4: the adaptive model's response-probability difference, D minus B,
# under both rules, with the chosen rule in ink. Figure 8c draws the same
# differences against completed updates; here the axis counts presentations,
# and the response on presentation q reflects q - 1 updates.
plot_response_gap <- function(r, rule, gamma = 8, theta = .5, mark = NULL) {
  rows <- lapply(c("sigmoid", "threshold"), function(f) {
    p_B <- response_prob(r$adaptive$B$V, f, gamma, theta)
    p_D <- response_prob(r$adaptive$D$V, f, gamma, theta)
    data.frame(rule = f, q = r$adaptive$B$k + 1, difference = p_D - p_B)
  })
  d <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  d <- d[d$q <= 10, ]
  d$chosen <- d$rule == rule
  lab <- c(sigmoid = "Sigmoid", threshold = "Threshold")
  ends <- d[d$q == max(d$q), ]
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(q, difference, group = rule)) +
    annotate("segment", x = 1, xend = 10, y = 0, yend = 0, colour = light, linewidth = .3) +
    geom_line(aes(colour = chosen, linewidth = chosen)) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = chosen), size = 1.4) +
    geom_text(data = ends, aes(label = lab[rule]), colour = ifelse(ends$chosen, ink, grey),
              hjust = 0, nudge_x = .3, size = 3.8) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = ink, `FALSE` = light)) +
    scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = .9, `FALSE` = .5)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 6, 10), expand = expansion(mult = c(.02, .02))) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-.05, 1.05), breaks = c(0, .5, 1), labels = c("0", ".5", "1")) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(1, 13), clip = "off") +
    labs(x = "Presentation", y = "Probability of a yes, D minus B",
         title = "Response difference in the adaptive model",
         subtitle = if (!is.null(mark)) "Dotted line: the presentation you chose") +
    theme_app()
  if (!is.null(mark)) p <- p + geom_vline(xintercept = mark, colour = grey, linewidth = .4,
                                          linetype = "dotted")
  p
}

# Step 5: answers of the first 24 participants in a case, colored as in
# Figure 9a. Presentations outside cols were not recorded.
plot_records <- function(case, cols = 1:10, rows = 1:24) {
  y <- case$y[rows, , drop = FALSE]
  d <- expand.grid(participant = seq_along(rows), col = 1:20)
  d$yes <- as.vector(y)
  d$cue <- ifelse(d$col <= 10, "B", "D")
  d$presentation <- ifelse(d$col <= 10, d$col, d$col - 10)
  d$fill <- ifelse(!(d$presentation %in% cols), "blank", ifelse(d$yes == 1, d$cue, "no"))
  ggplot(d, aes(presentation, participant)) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = fill), colour = "white", linewidth = .6) +
    facet_wrap(~cue, nrow = 1, labeller = as_labeller(c(B = "Answers to B", D = "Answers to D"))) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(no = "#C9C9C9", B = col_B, D = col_D, blank = "#FAFAFA")) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 5, 10), expand = expansion(0)) +
    scale_y_reverse(breaks = NULL, expand = expansion(0)) +
    labs(x = "Presentation", y = paste0("Participants 1–", length(rows)),
         subtitle = "Colored: yes · Gray: no · Blank: not recorded") +
    theme_app() +
    theme(axis.line = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())
}

# Step 5: the observed difference, yes to D minus yes to B, at each recorded
# presentation, with 95% intervals. With truth = TRUE it adds the generating
# probability difference as a wide grey line, as in Figure 9b.
plot_contrast <- function(case, design, truth = FALSE) {
  d <- design$by_presentation
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(presentation, estimate)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = light, linewidth = .3)
  if (truth) {
    generating <- data.frame(presentation = 1:10, difference = case$true_contrast)
    p <- p + geom_line(data = generating, aes(presentation, difference), colour = "#D4D4D4",
                       linewidth = 2.4, lineend = "round")
  }
  p + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), width = 0, colour = grey) +
    geom_point(size = 2.2, colour = ink) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10, limits = c(.5, 10.5)) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = axis_num) +
    expand_limits(y = c(-.2, .45)) +
    labs(x = "Presentation", y = "Yes to D minus yes to B",
         subtitle = if (truth)
           "Points: observed, with 95% intervals\nGray line: the generating probability difference"
         else "Observed response difference, with 95% intervals") +
    theme_app()
}

# Step 5: held-out log score of the carryover candidate minus each alternative,
# with bars two standard errors either side, as in Figure 9c.
plot_scores <- function(scores) {
  d <- scores
  # Keep a common scale for the saved cases, expanding it to include wider intervals.
  score_range <- range(-70, 130, 0, d$difference - 2 * d$se, d$difference + 2 * d$se)
  # ggplot draws the first level at the bottom, so listing reset first puts
  # fixed-rate at the top, as in Figure 9c.
  d$label <- factor(c(fixed = "Carryover minus\nfixed-rate", reset = "Carryover minus\nreset")[d$against],
                    levels = c("Carryover minus\nreset", "Carryover minus\nfixed-rate"))
  ggplot(d, aes(difference, label)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = light, linewidth = .3) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = difference - 2 * se, xmax = difference + 2 * se),
                  width = 0, colour = grey, linewidth = .8, orientation = "y") +
    geom_point(size = 3, colour = ink) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = score_range) +
    labs(x = "Difference in held-out\nlog score", y = NULL,
         subtitle = "Right of 0: carryover predicted better") +
    theme_app() +
    theme(axis.line.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())
}

# Explore: the response-probability difference, D minus B, for both models
# under the chosen rule.
plot_response_models <- function(r, rule, gamma, theta, second = "Adaptive model") {
  first <- "Rescorla–Wagner"
  rows <- lapply(c("rw", "adaptive"), function(m) data.frame(
    model = c(rw = first, adaptive = second)[[m]], q = r[[m]]$B$k + 1,
    difference = response_prob(r[[m]]$D$V, rule, gamma, theta) -
                 response_prob(r[[m]]$B$V, rule, gamma, theta)))
  d <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  d <- d[d$q <= 10, ]   # the answer on presentation q follows q - 1 updates
  d$model <- factor(d$model, levels = c(first, second))
  ends <- d[d$q == max(d$q), ]
  # The same scale as plot_response_gap(), extended only if a setting needs it.
  ylim <- range(-.05, 1.05, d$difference)
  ends$y <- spread_labels(ends$difference, .075 * diff(ylim))
  ggplot(d, aes(q, difference, colour = model, linetype = model)) +
    zero_line(max(d$q)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = .8) +
    geom_point(size = 1.6) +
    geom_text(data = ends, aes(y = y, label = model), hjust = 0, nudge_x = .3, size = 3.8) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(c(grey, ink), c(first, second))) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = setNames(c("22", "solid"), c(first, second))) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 5, 10), expand = expansion(mult = c(.02, .02))) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = axis_num) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(1, 15.5), ylim = ylim, clip = "off") +
    labs(x = "Presentation", y = "Probability of a yes, D minus B",
         title = "Response difference under the chosen rule") +
    theme_app()
}

# Step 6: decision-time densities of the two settings, with their means, as in
# Figure 12c. The labels are placed by hand beside their curves.
plot_ddm <- function(d = ddm_summary()) {
  times <- seq(0, 3.5, by = .005)
  curves <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(d)), function(i)
    data.frame(id = d$id[i], t = times, f = ddm_dens(times, d$v[i], d$a[i]))))
  means <- data.frame(id = d$id, t = d$mean,
                      f = vapply(seq_len(nrow(d)), function(i) ddm_dens(d$mean[i], d$v[i], d$a[i]), 0))
  mean_labels <- data.frame(id = d$id, x = c(1.3, .55), y = c(1.05, 2.3),
                            label = c(paste0("First setting: mean ", num0(d$mean[1], 2)),
                                      paste0("Second setting: mean ", num0(d$mean[2], 2))))
  ggplot(curves, aes(t, f, colour = id)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = .8) +
    geom_segment(data = means, aes(x = t, xend = t, y = 0, yend = f), linewidth = .4,
                 linetype = "22") +
    geom_text(data = mean_labels, aes(x, y, label = label), hjust = 0, size = 3.8,
              show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(first = ink, second = grey)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:3, expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .03))) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 3.5), clip = "off") +
    labs(x = "Decision time (model time units)", y = "Density",
         title = "Predicted decision times",
         subtitle = "Dashed lines mark the means") +
    theme_app()
}

# Step 4: from learned values to predicted responses (Section 4.4)
# The sigmoid and threshold rules applied to the adaptive model's learning
# curves of Step 2, the question whether more participants would reveal a
# difference, and further tries of a rule and a presentation.

responses_ui <- function() {
  scene("scene-4", "4", "What would you observe?", "output.done_q3c", "done_q4b",
    "A response function can preserve a difference in learned values, reduce it, or hide it at a given presentation.",
    p("How would the learned values appear in an experiment? Imagine using pictures
       as cues. You present B and D ten times each. Before each presentation's O2
       feedback, the participant answers “Do you expect O2?” A response function links
       the cue's current learned value to the probability of a yes. This is the
       observation bridge between the model and the recorded answer."),
    p("For this comparison, return to the adaptive model's curves from Step 2:
       no old-value carryover and full associability carryover. Keep those learning
       curves fixed while changing the response function. Each answer reflects learning
       before that presentation's feedback: the first comes before any O2 update,
       and the sixth comes after five updates."),
    p("Two response functions, each applied to both cues:"),
    tags$ul(
      tags$li(HTML("Under the sigmoid rule, the probability of a yes rises smoothly with learned
                    value and is .5 at a value of .5.")),
      tags$li(HTML("Under the threshold rule, the answer is yes whenever learned value is above
                    .5, and no otherwise."))),
    response_formulas_ui(),
    p(class = "muted", "Try both rules with these learning curves. The simulated
       experiment in the next step uses the sigmoid rule throughout, whichever rule
       you try here."),
    div(class = "question", uiOutput("q4a")),
    conditionalPanel("output.done_q4a",
      uiOutput("p4_values"),
      fig("p4_resp", "280px"),
      div(class = "question", uiOutput("q4b"))),
    conditionalPanel("output.done_q4b",
      div(class = "question small",
        p(class = "item-label", "Try another rule or presentation"),
        p(class = "muted", "Each try is added to the table below and to your notes."),
        div(class = "controls-inline",
          radioButtons("q4_try_rule", "Rule", inline = TRUE,
                       choices = c("Sigmoid" = "sigmoid", "Threshold" = "threshold")),
          radioButtons("q4_try_time", "Presentation", inline = TRUE,
                       choices = c("1" = "1", "6" = "6", "10" = "10"))),
        actionButton("q4_try_go", "Show", class = "btn-submit"),
        uiOutput("q4_tries")),
      aside("Section 4.4.")))
}


responses_server <- function(input, output, answers, add_note) {

  # The response functions
  rule_choices <- c(sigmoid = "Sigmoid", threshold = "Threshold")
  time_choices <- c(`1` = "Presentation 1 (before any update)",
                    `6` = "Presentation 6 (after five updates)",
                    `10` = "Presentation 10 (after nine updates)")
  test_points <- as.integer(names(time_choices))
  dir_choices <- c(D = "Higher for D", same = "The same", B = "Higher for B")
  peak_choices <- c(`1` = "At the first answer", `6` = "At the sixth", `10` = "At the last",
                    same = "The same at all three")
  peak_short <- c(`1` = "largest at the first answer", `6` = "largest at the sixth",
                  `10` = "largest at the last", same = "the same at all three")
  q4a_items <- list(
    item("rule", "Response function", rule_choices),
    item("time", "Which presentation will you look at?", time_choices),
    item("dir", "At this presentation, which cue has the higher probability of a yes?",
         dir_choices),
    item("peak", "Of presentations 1, 6 and 10, where do you expect the largest response difference?", peak_choices))

  # The adaptive model's learned values for O2, and the probabilities of a yes,
  # for B and D at presentation q under a response function. The answer on
  # presentation q reflects q - 1 updates.
  test_values <- function(rule, q) {
    q <- as.integer(q); k <- q - 1
    V_B <- at(ad_B$V, k); V_D <- at(ad_D$V, k)
    p_B <- response_prob(V_B, rule); p_D <- response_prob(V_D, rule)
    d <- p_D - p_B
    list(rule = rule, q = q, k = k, V_B = V_B, V_D = V_D, p_B = p_B, p_D = p_D, d = d,
         dir = if (abs(d) < 1e-12) "same" else if (d > 0) "D" else "B")
  }
  # The response differences at presentations 1, 6 and 10, and where the
  # largest is ("same" when all three are equal).
  largest_at <- function(rule) {
    d <- vapply(test_points, function(q) test_values(rule, q)$d, numeric(1))
    top <- as.character(test_points[abs(d - max(d)) < 1e-12])
    list(d = d, top = if (length(top) == length(test_points)) "same" else top)
  }
  test_set <- function(rule, q)
    paste0(first_set(), "; ", rule_set(rule), "; presentation ", q,
           "; response before feedback, after ", as.integer(q) - 1, " updates")
  nth_answer <- function(q) c(`1` = "the first answer", `6` = "the sixth answer",
                              `10` = "the last answer")[[as.character(q)]]
  # The presentations on which the threshold rule answers differently for B and
  # D: B's value at or below .5 and D's above it (Equation 20).
  threshold_window <- which(at(ad_B$V, 0:9) <= .5 & at(ad_D$V, 0:9) > .5)

  ask_server("q4a", input, output, answers, q4a_items, button = "See the predicted responses",
    feedback = function(a) {
      v <- test_values(a$rule, a$time)
      pattern <- largest_at(a$rule)
      rule <- tolower(rule_choices[[a$rule]])
      tagList(
        if (a$dir != v$dir) {
          expected <- if (a$dir == "same") "You expected equal yes probabilities. " else
            paste0("You expected a higher probability of a yes for ", a$dir, ". ")
          P(expected,
            if (v$k == 0)
              "Neither cue has received O2 feedback yet. Both start at value 0,
               and the same response function gives them the same yes probability."
            else if (v$dir == "same")
              "D has the higher learned value, but both values are above .5.
               The threshold gives a yes for either cue, hiding their difference."
            else if (a$dir == "B")
              "D has the higher learned value. This response function never gives a
               lower value a higher yes probability, so it cannot put B ahead."
            else if (a$rule == "sigmoid")
              "D has the higher learned value, and the sigmoid increases with
               value. The two yes probabilities therefore differ."
            else
              "D's value is above .5 while B's is at or below .5. The threshold
               therefore gives a yes for D and a no for B.")
        },
        P("At ", nth_answer(v$q), " (",
          if (v$k == 0) "before any update" else paste0("after ", updates(v$k)),
          "), ", if (v$V_D == v$V_B) "B and D have the same learned value" else
            paste0("D's learned value is ahead by ", prob(v$V_D - v$V_B)),
          ". The ", rule, " rule turns that into ",
          if (v$dir != "same")
            paste0("a difference of ", prob(v$d), " in the probability of a yes.")
          else if (v$p_B %in% c(0, 1))
            paste0("the same answer for both cues: every participant answers ",
                   if (v$p_B == 0) "no" else "yes", " to B and to D.")
          else paste0("the same probability of a yes for both cues, ", prob(v$p_B), ".")),
        if (!(a$peak %in% pattern$top))
          p(switch(a$peak,
            `1` = "You expected the largest difference at the first answer.
              Associability affects learning from feedback; it does not give either
              cue an O2 value before that feedback. Both start at 0, so the first
              response probabilities are equal.",
            `10` = if (a$rule == "sigmoid")
              "You expected the largest difference at the last answer. By then,
               D's yes probability is near the ceiling while B's is rising through
               the steep middle, bringing the probabilities closer. At the sixth
               presentation, B's value is below the midpoint and D's above it, where
               the sigmoid is steepest."
              else "You expected the largest difference at the last answer.
               By then both values are above .5, so the threshold gives a yes for
               both. At the sixth presentation, the values fall on opposite sides
               of the threshold.",
            same = if (a$rule == "sigmoid")
              "You expected the same response difference at all three presentations.
               Both the values and their position on the sigmoid change during
               learning, so the response difference changes too."
              else "You expected the same response difference at all three presentations.
               The threshold gives the same answer for both cues at the first and
               last presentations, but different answers at the sixth.")),
        P("Under the ", rule, " rule the difference is ", prob(pattern$d[1]),
          " at the first answer, ", prob(pattern$d[2]), " at the sixth and ",
          prob(pattern$d[3]), " at the last, so it is ",
          if (identical(pattern$top, "same")) "the same at all three." else
            paste0(peak_short[[pattern$top[1]]], ".")),
        p(if (a$rule == "sigmoid") "The sigmoid is steepest at learned value .5.
            A difference in values is easier to see in responses near that midpoint
            than near the floor or ceiling."
          else paste0("The threshold rule gives different answers only when B is at or below
            .5 and D above it. That happens only on presentations ",
            min(threshold_window), " to ", max(threshold_window), ". Before that both cues
            are below .5, and afterward both are above it.")))
    },
    on_submit = function(a) {
      v <- test_values(a$rule, a$time)
      pattern <- largest_at(a$rule)
      add_note("Step 4", "Response function",
        paste0("Presentation ", v$q, " with the ", tolower(rule_choices[[a$rule]]),
               " rule. Is the probability of a yes higher for D than for B? Where is the",
               " difference largest?"),
        paste0(dir_choices[[a$dir]], ". ", peak_choices[[a$peak]], "."),
        result = paste0("Probability of a yes ", prob(v$p_B), " for B and ",
          prob(v$p_D), " for D, a difference of ", prob(v$d), " (learned values ", prob(v$V_B),
          " and ", prob(v$V_D), "). The difference is ", prob(pattern$d[1]),
          " at the first answer, ", prob(pattern$d[2]), " at the sixth and ",
          prob(pattern$d[3]), " at the last."),
        settings = test_set(a$rule, v$q))
    })

  output$p4_values <- renderUI({
    req(answers$q4a)
    v <- test_values(answers$q4a$rule, answers$q4a$time)
    tagList(tags$table(class = "values",
      tags$thead(tags$tr(tags$th(""), tags$th(class = "cue-B", "B"),
                         tags$th(class = "cue-D", "D"), tags$th("D minus B"))),
      tags$tbody(
        tags$tr(tags$td(paste0("Learned value at presentation ", v$q)),
                tags$td(prob(v$V_B)), tags$td(prob(v$V_D)), tags$td(prob(v$V_D - v$V_B))),
        tags$tr(tags$td("Probability of a yes"), tags$td(prob(v$p_B)),
                tags$td(prob(v$p_D)), tags$td(prob(v$d))))),
      p(class = "table-note", "Differences are calculated from unrounded values."))
  })
  output$p4_resp <- renderPlot({
    req(answers$q4a)
    plot_response_gap(base, answers$q4a$rule, mark = as.integer(answers$q4a$time))
  })

  q4b_items <- list(item("more",
    "Under this rule, could more participants at this presentation reveal the learned-value difference in their responses?",
    c(yes = "Yes.", no = "No.")))
  ask_server("q4b", input, output, answers, q4b_items,
    feedback = function(a) {
      v <- test_values(answers$q4a$rule, answers$q4a$time)
      right <- if (v$dir == "same") "no" else "yes"
      certain <- right == "yes" && all(c(v$p_B, v$p_D) %in% c(0, 1))
      tagList(
        if (a$more == "yes" && right == "no")
          p("A larger sample can reduce sampling noise. It cannot change the fact
            that this rule gives both cues the same response probability.")
        else if (a$more == "no" && right == "yes")
          p("Here the rule does preserve a response difference."),
        p(if (v$V_D == v$V_B) "At this presentation B and D have the same learned value, so
            there is no difference for more participants to reveal. A later presentation could show one."
          else if (right == "no") "Under this rule B and D have the same probability of a yes at
            this presentation. More participants cannot recover a difference that the
            measure does not express. Another presentation, or a different measure, could."
          else if (certain) paste0("Under this rule every participant answers ",
            if (v$p_B == 0) "no" else "yes", " to B and ", if (v$p_D == 0) "no" else "yes",
            " to D at this presentation, so even a few participants show the difference.")
          else paste0("The two probabilities differ by ", num(v$d), ". Each answer is a
            random draw, so in a finite sample D need not get more yes answers than B. With
            more participants, the difference is estimated more precisely.")))
    },
    on_submit = function(a) {
      v <- test_values(answers$q4a$rule, answers$q4a$time)
      add_note("Step 4", "More participants",
        "Under this rule, could more participants reveal the learned-value difference in their responses?",
        q4b_items[[1]]$choices[[a$more]],
        result = paste0("Probability of a yes ", prob(v$p_B), " for B and ",
                        prob(v$p_D), " for D at this presentation, a difference of ", prob(v$d), "."),
        settings = test_set(v$rule, v$q))
    })

  q4_tries <- reactiveVal(list())
  observeEvent(input$q4_try_go, {
    req(answers$q4a, input$q4_try_rule, input$q4_try_time)
    v <- test_values(input$q4_try_rule, input$q4_try_time)
    q4_tries(c(q4_tries(), list(v)))
    add_note("Step 4", "Another rule or presentation",
      paste0(rule_choices[[v$rule]], " rule, presentation ", v$q, "."),
      "Viewed.",
      result = paste0("Probability of a yes ", prob(v$p_B), " for B and ",
                      prob(v$p_D), " for D, a difference of ", prob(v$d), "."),
      settings = test_set(v$rule, v$q))
  })
  output$q4_tries <- renderUI({
    tries <- q4_tries()
    if (!length(tries)) return(NULL)
    tagList(
      p(class = "table-note", "Probability of a yes at the presentation"),
      div(class = "scroll-x", tabindex = "0", role = "region",
          `aria-label` = "Probabilities of a yes for each try", tags$table(class = "values",
        tags$thead(tags$tr(tags$th("Rule"), tags$th("Presentation"),
                           tags$th(class = "cue-B", "B"), tags$th(class = "cue-D", "D"),
                           tags$th("D minus B"))),
        tags$tbody(lapply(tries, function(v) tags$tr(
          tags$td(rule_choices[[v$rule]]), tags$td(v$q), tags$td(prob(v$p_B)),
          tags$td(prob(v$p_D)), tags$td(prob(v$d))))))),
      p(class = "table-note", "Differences are calculated from unrounded values."))
  })

  # Starting the inquiry again clears the answers and the tries but keeps the
  # notes.
  list(reset = function() {
    clear_answers(answers, c("q4a", "q4b"))
    q4_tries(list())
  })
}

# The model results the page shows, computed once when the app starts. Shiny
# sources the files in R/ in alphabetical order, so this file comes after
# engine.R, which defines the functions used here.

base     <- run_inquiry(default_settings)
trained  <- base$trained
trace    <- compound_trace(default_settings)
n_base   <- default_settings$n_compound
n_more   <- 30                               # compound trials in Step 2's longer training
more     <- trained_states(settings_with(n_compound = n_more))
co       <- continue_o1(default_settings)
# The gaps after eight updates as g_V varies, and the g_V at which the two
# models' gaps are equal (Figure 7a; the curves cross once, between .5 and 1).
gv_grid  <- gap_by_value_carryover(k = 8)
gv_cross <- uniroot(function(g) {
  r <- run_inquiry(settings_with(g_V = g))
  r$rw$gap[9] - r$adaptive$gap[9]
}, c(.5, 1), tol = 1e-8)$root
gv1      <- run_inquiry(settings_with(g_V = 1))
# Half of the associability change carried over to O2 (Section 4.3).
ga_half  <- run_inquiry(settings_with(g_alpha = .5))
# E one part in a million more or less salient than D (Section 4.5).
e_up     <- run_inquiry(settings_with(e_offset = 1e-6))
e_down   <- run_inquiry(settings_with(e_offset = -1e-6))
peak_k   <- which.max(base$adaptive$gap) - 1
at       <- function(x, k) x[k + 1]          # value after k completed updates
ad_B     <- base$adaptive$B
ad_D     <- base$adaptive$D

# The simulated experiments of Step 5, written by shiny_app/make_inference_cases.R.
inference   <- readRDS("data/inference_cases.rds")
cases       <- inference$cases
rates       <- inference$rates
zero_rates  <- inference$zero_rates
first_rates <- inference$first_rates

content:
# Simulated experiments for Step 5 of the companion app. In the app, the reader
# designs the experiment: 40 or 160 participants, and the last three, the first
# six, or all ten presentations recorded. For each of three generating
# processes, this script takes one experiment of each size from the Section 5
# study, regenerates its records from the saved seed, and analyzes them under
# each design. The response contrast and the held-out comparison of the three
# candidates, with old-value carryover estimated and with it fixed at 0, use the
# study's functions in R/inference.R; the first-answer check repeats the test of
# analysis/section5_first_response_and_bounds.R. Where the study saved the same
# analysis, the script stops unless the two agree. The study ran the comparison
# with old-value carryover fixed at 0 only for carried associability and value
# generalization, with 160 participants and all ten presentations; the other
# fixed-at-0 analyses are made here. Writes shiny_app/data/inference_cases.rds.
#   Rscript shiny_app/make_inference_cases.R   (about half a minute)
#
# Selection: for each process, the first experiment of each size in the
# study's first configuration. The value-generalization experiment with 160
# participants is also the first in that configuration in which the fixed-at-0
# comparison favored associability carryover; the app says so when it reveals
# the process, and reports how often that happened across all 400 experiments.

if (!file.exists("R/inference.R")) stop("Run this script from the repository root.")
source("R/inference.R")

study_dir <- "results/section5"
jobs <- read.csv(file.path(study_dir, "jobs.csv"))
generating <- read.csv(file.path(study_dir, "generating_parameters.csv"))
saved <- read.csv(file.path(study_dir, "results.csv"))
study <- read.csv(file.path(study_dir, "summary.csv"))
first_checks <- read.csv(file.path(study_dir, "initial_response_checks.csv"))
first_summary <- read.csv(file.path(study_dir, "initial_response_summary.csv"))

sources <- c("value", "associability", "reset")
sizes <- c(40L, 160L)
views <- c("late", "early", "full")
view_cols <- list(late = 8:10, early = 1:6, full = 1:10)
# The app's names for the two choices of g_V, and the study's.
policies <- c(estimated = "value_allowed", zero = "value_zero")

first_in_config1 <- function(scenario, n) {
  min(saved$id[saved$scenario == scenario & saved$n == n & saved$config == 1 &
                 saved$view == "full" & saved$policy == "value_allowed"])
}
stopifnot(first_in_config1("value", 160) ==
  min(saved$id[saved$scenario == "value" & saved$n == 160 & saved$config == 1 &
                 saved$policy == "value_zero" & saved$decision == "carry"]))

# Section 5.6: the exact one-sided paired test of equal first answers to B
# (column 1) and D (column n_pres + 1). Among the participants whose two first
# answers differ, the number who answer yes to D only is binomial with
# probability .5 under equality.
first_response_check <- function(y, n_pres = 10L) {
  d_only <- sum(y[, n_pres + 1L] == 1 & y[, 1L] == 0)
  b_only <- sum(y[, n_pres + 1L] == 0 & y[, 1L] == 1)
  discordant <- d_only + b_only
  p <- if (discordant == 0) 1 else pbinom(d_only - 1, discordant, .5, lower.tail = FALSE)
  list(d_only = d_only, b_only = b_only, p = p, n = nrow(y))
}

# The D-minus-B difference in yes proportions at each recorded presentation q,
# with the interval of Figure 9b (Agresti and Min, 2005): add 1/2 to each cell
# of the paired 2 x 2 table, then use the Wald interval for the difference of
# the two discordant proportions. These are the points and bars of the app's
# contrast plot.
contrast_by_presentation <- function(y, cols, n_pres = 10L) {
  n <- nrow(y)
  t(vapply(cols, function(q) {
    n_d_only <- sum(y[, n_pres + q] == 1 & y[, q] == 0)
    n_b_only <- sum(y[, q] == 1 & y[, n_pres + q] == 0)
    p_d <- (n_d_only + .5) / (n + 2)
    p_b <- (n_b_only + .5) / (n + 2)
    se <- sqrt((p_d + p_b - (p_d - p_b)^2) / (n + 2))
    c(presentation = q, estimate = (n_d_only - n_b_only) / n,
      lower = p_d - p_b - qnorm(.975) * se, upper = p_d - p_b + qnorm(.975) * se)
  }, numeric(4)))
}

# The carryover candidate's held-out score minus that of each alternative, with
# its standard error.
score_table <- function(comparison) {
  scores <- as.data.frame(comparison$carry_contrasts)
  scores$against <- rownames(scores)
  rownames(scores) <- NULL
  scores[, c("against", "difference", "se")]
}

# The analyses of one design, which use only the recorded presentations. The
# comparisons are returned for the checks against the study and dropped before
# saving.
analyze <- function(observed, view) {
  recorded <- inference_view(observed, view)
  comparisons <- list(estimated = inference_compare(recorded, value = TRUE),
                      zero = inference_compare(recorded, value = FALSE))
  list(cols = view_cols[[view]],
       effect = inference_effect(recorded),
       by_presentation = as.data.frame(contrast_by_presentation(observed$y, view_cols[[view]])),
       scores = lapply(comparisons, score_table),
       decision = lapply(comparisons, `[[`, "decision"),
       first = if (1L %in% view_cols[[view]]) first_response_check(observed$y) else NULL,
       comparisons = comparisons)
}

cases <- list()
for (src in sources) for (n in sizes) {
  id <- first_in_config1(src, n)
  job <- jobs[jobs$id == id, ]
  setting <- generating[generating$scenario == src & generating$config == job$config, ]
  par <- unlist(setting[inference_names])
  generated <- inference_generate(job$n, par, setting$adaptive, job$seed)
  observed <- generated$observed
  truth_p <- generated$truth$probability

  designs <- lapply(views, function(view) analyze(observed, view))
  names(designs) <- views

  # Agreement with the study, wherever it saved the same analysis.
  for (view in views) for (policy in names(policies)) {
    row <- saved[saved$id == id & saved$view == view & saved$policy == policies[[policy]], ]
    if (!nrow(row)) next
    comparison <- designs[[view]]$comparisons[[policy]]
    effect <- designs[[view]]$effect
    stopifnot(nrow(row) == 1,
              abs(effect[["estimate"]] - row$estimate) < 1e-9,
              abs(effect[["lower"]] - row$lower) < 1e-9, abs(effect[["upper"]] - row$upper) < 1e-9,
              effect[["detected"]] == row$detected,
              abs(comparison$carry_contrasts["fixed", "difference"] - row$carry_vs_fixed) < 5e-5,
              abs(comparison$carry_contrasts["reset", "difference"] - row$carry_vs_reset) < 5e-5,
              identical(comparison$decision, row$decision))
  }
  # The study made the first-answer check for every experiment.
  first <- designs$full$first
  saved_first <- first_checks[first_checks$id == id, ]
  stopifnot(first$d_only == saved_first$discordant_control,
            first$b_only == saved_first$discordant_blocked,
            abs(first$p - saved_first$initial_p) < 1e-12)
  for (view in views) designs[[view]]$comparisons <- NULL

  # true_contrast is the generating D-minus-B difference in the probability of a
  # yes at each presentation, averaged over the participants.
  cases[[src]][[as.character(n)]] <- list(
    id = id, seed = job$seed, n = job$n, source = src, config = job$config,
    generating = as.list(par),
    y = observed$y, allocation = observed$allocation,
    true_contrast = colMeans(truth_p[, 11:20] - truth_p[, 1:10]),
    designs = designs)
  cat(sprintf("%s, %d participants: experiment %d analyzed under %d designs\n",
              src, n, id, length(views)))
}
